fixSteps.title: Check wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Verify connector at sensor and at BCM side.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new rain/light sensor module.

faq.q: Why after a windshield swap?
faq.a: The gel pad that couples the sensor to the glass must be perfectly bubble-free.

title: Left Headlight Ballast/Driver Fault
shortDescription: The left HID ballast or LED driver module is reporting a fault.
fullDescription:
Code B2290 indicates that the left headlight's high-voltage ballast (HID) or constant-current driver (LED) has failed or is reporting an overcurrent/undercurrent condition. The module steps up 12V to the thousands of volts needed by HID lamps or regulates precise current for LED chips.

Common failures are thermal fatigue of internal capacitors (HID ballasts), moisture intrusion, or a shorted bulb/LED array pulling the driver into protection. A bad bulb is often the root cause — replacing the ballast without the bulb leads to repeat failure.

The affected headlight will either not illuminate or flicker.
safetyImpact: Reduced forward visibility — one headlight out.

causes.cause: Failed HID bulb triggering ballast shutdown

fixSteps.title: Swap bulb/module side-to-side
fixSteps.instruction: Move suspect bulb to opposite side — fault follows bulb if bulb is bad.

fixSteps.title: Check ballast
fixSteps.instruction: Measure secondary voltage with HID-rated meter, or watch DTC on LED driver.

fixSteps.title: Replace component
fixSteps.instruction: Install new ballast or LED driver and bulb as needed.

faq.q: Why replace bulb with ballast?
faq.a: A failing bulb caused the ballast to fail — reusing it kills the new ballast.

title: Right Headlight Ballast/Driver Fault
shortDescription: The right HID ballast or LED driver is reporting a fault.
fullDescription:
Code B2295 is the right-side counterpart to B2290. It indicates the driver electronics for the right headlight have detected an internal fault, overcurrent, or bulb failure.

Diagnosis and repair mirror the left side — confirm whether the bulb or driver is at fault by swapping, then replace as needed.

On matrix LED headlights, a single failed LED chip can set this code even if the rest of the lamp works — the whole headlight assembly may need replacement because the chips are not field-serviceable.
safetyImpact: Reduced forward visibility — one headlight out.

fixSteps.title: Swap bulb
fixSteps.instruction: Test by swapping bulb left-right.

fixSteps.title: Test driver
fixSteps.instruction: Check LED driver or HID ballast output.

fixSteps.title: Replace component
fixSteps.instruction: Install new bulb or driver module.

faq.q: Matrix LED chip failure?
faq.a: Yes — often requires full headlight housing on premium LED systems.

title: Adaptive Headlight Leveling Motor Fault
shortDescription: The automatic headlight leveling motor is not reaching commanded position.
fullDescription:
Code B2600 indicates that the small stepper motor that aims the headlight up and down based on suspension load has stalled, lost position feedback, or is not being commanded correctly. Most HID- or LED-equipped vehicles are legally required to have auto-leveling so the beam does not blind oncoming traffic when the rear is loaded.

Failures come from water in the motor, a seized ball-joint on the leveling rod, or a bad height sensor feeding the BCM. When leveling fails, the beam defaults to a safe low position, giving poor forward visibility at night.

Replacing the leveling motor usually requires removal of the headlight housing.
safetyImpact: Headlight aimed too low or too high — reduced night visibility or glare to oncoming traffic.

fixSteps.title: Check height sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Verify front/rear height sensor output with scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Command motor
fixSteps.instruction: Actuate leveling motor and watch for movement.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove headlight housing, replace leveling motor assembly.

faq.q: Can I disable leveling?
faq.a: No — it's a regulated safety function and will set a fault if disconnected.

title: Left Front Side Airbag Deployment Control Circuit
shortDescription: SRS module detected a fault in the left front side (thorax) airbag firing circuit.
fullDescription:
Code B0010 indicates the Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) module has measured an out-of-range resistance in the left front side airbag squib circuit. The module performs a low-current integrity test at key-on and at regular intervals — if the loop resistance falls outside the factory window (typically 1.5-5 ohms), the code latches and the airbag warning lamp stays on.

The side airbag lives inside the driver's seat or door trim; its connector is a yellow shorting-type connector under the seat. Bad pins, moisture, or a pinched harness from a seat rail are the usual failure points.

Do NOT probe the squib with a regular multimeter — use only an SRS-rated load tool or you risk deployment.
safetyImpact: Left side airbag will not deploy in a side-impact collision.

causes.cause: Pinched/chafed airbag harness from seat rail

fixSteps.title: Disable SRS
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect battery and wait 10 minutes before touching any SRS component.

fixSteps.title: Inspect seat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Slide seat fully forward and back, inspect the yellow connector and loom for chafing.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector or replace jumper
fixSteps.instruction: Clean pins, reseat. If harness is damaged, replace the under-seat SRS jumper.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive?
faq.a: The other airbags still work, but the side airbag will not deploy — repair promptly.

title: Right Front Side Airbag Deployment Circuit
shortDescription: SRS detected fault in right front side airbag firing loop.
fullDescription:
Code B0012 is the passenger-side counterpart to B0010. The SRS module has lost the expected resistance signature on the right front thorax airbag squib. Because the passenger seat moves often and the harness runs through the seat frame, this is one of the most common SRS codes on aging vehicles.

Corrosion at the yellow under-seat connector is the #1 cause, followed by a broken wire from seat fore/aft travel. In rare cases the airbag module itself has failed internally.

After repair, codes must be cleared with a scan tool that supports SRS — a simple code reader will not reset the airbag lamp.
safetyImpact: Passenger side airbag disabled in a side-impact crash.

fixSteps.title: Power down SRS
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect battery, wait 10 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Pop yellow connector under passenger seat — look for green corrosion or bent pins.

fixSteps.title: Repair and clear
fixSteps.instruction: Repair connector or jumper, then clear codes with SRS-capable scanner.

faq.q: Can I clear this with a cheap scanner?
faq.a: No — SRS modules require a capable bidirectional scan tool to clear.

title: Left Curtain Airbag Deployment Control
shortDescription: Fault detected in left side curtain (roof-rail) airbag circuit.
fullDescription:
Code B0013 indicates the SRS module cannot verify the firing loop for the left side curtain airbag, which is mounted along the headliner from A-pillar to C-pillar. This airbag deploys downward to protect occupants' heads in side impacts and rollovers.

Because the curtain airbag harness is hidden behind the headliner and pillar trim, faults usually come from connector damage during other repairs (windshield replacement, sunroof service) or from moisture intrusion at the A-pillar.

Repair requires removing pillar trim carefully — clips break easily and pillar trim contains its own tear seams for deployment.
safetyImpact: Curtain airbag disabled — major risk in rollover or side impact.

causes.cause: Damaged connector at A-pillar from prior trim work

fixSteps.title: Disable SRS
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect battery and wait 10 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Remove A-pillar trim
fixSteps.instruction: Carefully pop A-pillar trim — note tear seams for deployment.

fixSteps.title: Inspect & repair harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check connector and wiring for corrosion/damage; repair or replace.

faq.q: Why after windshield replacement?
faq.a: Glass techs often pull A-pillar trim and can damage the SRS connector.

title: Right Curtain Airbag Deployment Control
shortDescription: Fault detected in right side curtain airbag firing circuit.
fullDescription:
Code B0014 is the passenger-side curtain airbag fault, mirroring B0013. The SRS module has detected an open, short, or out-of-range resistance at the right roof-rail curtain airbag squib.

Common sources: trim clips that pinch the harness after A-pillar removal, water leaks from a plugged sunroof drain running down the A-pillar, or damage during seatbelt pretensioner service.

Because curtain airbags protect the head area — the most injury-prone region in side crashes — any fault here is high-priority.
safetyImpact: Right curtain airbag will not deploy — increased head injury risk.

causes.cause: Water from sunroof drain corroding connector

fixSteps.title: Depower SRS
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect battery, 10-minute wait.

fixSteps.title: Check sunroof drains
fixSteps.instruction: Verify A-pillar sunroof drain is clear — flush with distilled water.

fixSteps.title: Inspect/repair harness
fixSteps.instruction: Remove A-pillar trim and inspect curtain airbag connector.

faq.q: Water caused this?
faq.a: Yes — clogged sunroof drains are a top cause of A-pillar SRS faults.

title: Driver Seatbelt Pretensioner Circuit
shortDescription: SRS detected fault in driver seatbelt pretensioner squib circuit.
fullDescription:
Code B0015 indicates the driver's seatbelt pretensioner — the pyrotechnic device that yanks belt slack out in a crash — has an invalid resistance on its firing loop. Pretensioners share the SRS bus with airbags and are tested the same way.

This fault typically arises after seat or B-pillar work — the pretensioner connector at the belt retractor base gets disturbed. Some pretensioners also include a load-limiter sensor that can fail independently.

A pretensioner cannot be repaired — if the squib itself is bad, the whole belt retractor assembly is replaced.
safetyImpact: Belt will not tighten in a crash — reduced occupant protection.

causes.cause: Damaged harness at seat belt base

fixSteps.title: Power down
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect battery, 10 min wait.

fixSteps.title: Check connector
fixSteps.instruction: Remove B-pillar trim, locate pretensioner yellow connector, verify seating.

fixSteps.title: Replace if needed
fixSteps.instruction: If squib resistance is out of spec, replace belt assembly.

faq.q: Can I buy a used belt?
faq.a: Not recommended — a used pretensioner may have partially fired in a crash.

title: Passenger Seatbelt Pretensioner Circuit
shortDescription: Fault in passenger seatbelt pretensioner firing loop.
fullDescription:
Code B0018 indicates the SRS module cannot verify the passenger pretensioner squib circuit. Like the driver side, failure commonly traces to the yellow connector at the B-pillar or a harness pinched by the seat belt retractor bolt.

On vehicles with buckle pretensioners (inside the buckle end rather than the retractor), a separate code B0020 may set instead, but the two often appear together.

Do not use standard meters to probe the squib — only use SRS loaders from the factory test equipment.
safetyImpact: Passenger belt will not pre-tension in a crash.

fixSteps.title: Disable SRS
fixSteps.instruction: Battery off, wait 10 min.

fixSteps.title: Remove B-pillar trim
fixSteps.instruction: Access pretensioner connector and inspect.

fixSteps.title: Replace belt if needed
fixSteps.instruction: Swap retractor assembly if internal squib bad.

faq.q: Is this a recall item?
faq.a: Some vehicles have pretensioner recalls — check your VIN on the NHTSA site.

title: Driver Buckle Pretensioner Circuit
shortDescription: Buckle-end pretensioner on driver belt shows circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B0020 is set when a buckle pretensioner — the kind that pulls the buckle-end down into the seat rather than yanking the retractor — has an out-of-range squib reading. Buckle pretensioners are common on newer vehicles with integrated belts on bolster seats.

The pretensioner lives under the seat cushion on an articulated arm and connects through a small yellow SRS connector. Seat cushion removal, aftermarket seat covers, or child seat installation can disturb the connector.

After repair, use a bidirectional scan tool to clear the SRS memory.
safetyImpact: Buckle will not pull down in crash — reduced belt effectiveness.

fixSteps.title: Depower SRS
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect battery, wait 10 min.

fixSteps.title: Inspect under seat
fixSteps.instruction: Lift seat cushion, check buckle pretensioner connector.

fixSteps.title: Repair or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat connector, replace buckle assembly if squib bad.

faq.q: Seat covers caused this?
faq.a: Sometimes — if they pinch the yellow harness routing under the cushion.

title: Passenger Buckle Pretensioner Circuit
shortDescription: Passenger-side buckle pretensioner circuit out of range.
fullDescription:
Code B0024 indicates the passenger buckle pretensioner squib has an invalid resistance. It is the right-side counterpart of B0020.

Troubleshooting is identical: inspect the under-seat SRS connector, verify harness routing, and replace the buckle assembly if the squib itself has failed. Many vehicles use a slightly different connector color-code on the passenger side to avoid cross-wiring.

Also check for the occupant classification system — disturbing the seat wiring can set multiple codes at once.
safetyImpact: Passenger buckle will not tighten in a crash.

fixSteps.title: Battery off
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect battery, wait 10 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Under-seat inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Access passenger buckle harness under seat cushion.

fixSteps.title: Repair
fixSteps.instruction: Fix connector or replace buckle assembly.

faq.q: Why did it appear after a child seat install?
faq.a: Shoving the LATCH anchor or seat itself can disturb harness routing.

title: Knee Airbag Deployment Circuit
shortDescription: SRS detected fault in driver knee airbag squib circuit.
fullDescription:
Code B0028 indicates the driver knee airbag — mounted under the steering column in the lower dash — has an invalid firing loop. Knee airbags prevent submarining (sliding under the belt) and reduce lower-leg injuries.

Failures often trace to lower dash work: replacing the OBD-II connector, removing the brake pedal, or knee bolster reinstallation. The squib connector is yellow and mounts to a bracket behind the knee bolster panel.

If the squib resistance is bad, replace the entire knee airbag unit.
safetyImpact: Driver knee airbag disabled — increased lower-body injury risk.

causes.cause: Connector disturbed during lower dash work

fixSteps.title: Disable SRS
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect battery, 10 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Remove knee bolster
fixSteps.instruction: Pop off lower dash panel, access knee airbag harness.

fixSteps.title: Repair/replace
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat connector or replace airbag module.

faq.q: Do all cars have knee airbags?
faq.a: No — they are more common on mid/premium trims and specific markets.

title: Occupant Classification System Malfunction
shortDescription: Passenger seat occupant classification system reports invalid weight data.
fullDescription:
Code B0090 indicates the passenger Occupant Classification System (OCS) — a bladder or strain-gauge array under the seat — is reporting implausible data. OCS decides whether to enable the passenger airbag and at what power level (full, partial, suppressed) based on occupant weight.

Common causes are a cracked sensor mat, aftermarket seat covers altering weight distribution, or loose seat mounting bolts. The passenger airbag status lamp will show OFF or blink as a diagnostic indicator.

OCS usually requires a re-zero calibration after any seat service — the module learns the unoccupied weight as baseline.
safetyImpact: Passenger airbag may deploy for a child or not deploy for an adult.

fixSteps.title: Verify bolts
fixSteps.instruction: Torque all four seat mounting bolts to spec.

fixSteps.title: Remove seat covers
fixSteps.instruction: Temporarily remove aftermarket cover and clear codes.

fixSteps.title: Re-zero OCS
fixSteps.instruction: Perform OCS zero/rezero routine via factory scan tool.

faq.q: Do seat covers really cause this?
faq.a: Yes — some heavy covers shift the load path on the sensor mat.

title: Passenger Seat Pressure Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: Pressure sensor in passenger seat reports out-of-range signal.
fullDescription:
Code B0091 indicates the bladder-style pressure sensor in the passenger seat is giving a signal outside the expected range. Some OCS designs use a fluid-filled bladder with a pressure transducer; a pinhole leak will drop the reading, and the code latches.

This is distinct from B0090 (overall OCS fault) — B0091 points specifically to the sensor itself, often requiring a seat cushion replacement kit that includes the bladder and transducer as a matched set.

Recalibration is mandatory after parts replacement.
safetyImpact: Airbag deploy decision compromised for the passenger.

fixSteps.title: Scan for codes
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm B0091 specifically vs B0090.

fixSteps.title: Inspect bladder
fixSteps.instruction: Remove passenger seat cushion, inspect bladder for fluid leaks.

fixSteps.title: Replace cushion kit
fixSteps.instruction: Install new bladder/transducer assembly as a matched set.

faq.q: Can the bladder be patched?
faq.a: No — it must be replaced as a calibrated assembly.

title: Passenger Classification Module Calibration Lost
shortDescription: OCS module has lost zero-point calibration.
fullDescription:
Code B0092 is set when the passenger classification module has lost its baseline (unoccupied) calibration. This can happen after battery disconnect, module replacement, or a sharp impact to the seat. Until re-calibrated, the module defaults to passenger airbag OFF for safety.

Re-zero requires the seat fully empty, no objects in the footwell under the seat, and use of a factory-level scan tool's special function. Some scanners from aftermarket brands also support it (Autel, Launch X431).

After a successful re-zero, the airbag lamp should clear within one drive cycle.
safetyImpact: Passenger airbag forced OFF until calibration completes.

fixSteps.title: Empty seat
fixSteps.instruction: Remove all items from passenger seat and floor.

fixSteps.title: Run rezero
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool Special Function → OCS Zero Calibration.

fixSteps.title: Verify
fixSteps.instruction: Sit in seat, confirm ON/OFF lamp changes correctly.

faq.q: Will the code clear itself?
faq.a: No — zeroing must be done with a scan tool.

title: Driver Seat Position Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Memory seat position sensor returning invalid data.
fullDescription:
Code B0156 indicates the seat module cannot read a valid signal from one of the Hall-effect or potentiometer sensors tracking seat fore/aft, recline, or height. Without valid position, the memory seat feature cannot recall presets.

On most vehicles, sensors live inside the seat motors themselves. A worn pigtail at the seat rail, a stripped gear, or water damage from spilled drinks are common causes.

Some makes (GM, Ford) will disable the entire memory system until the fault clears.
safetyImpact: Memory presets unavailable; seat still moves manually.

fixSteps.title: Scan and locate
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan data to identify which axis (fore/aft vs recline) is faulting.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Remove seat, trace axis harness, look for chafing or corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap seat motor assembly if sensor is internal failure.

faq.q: Can I replace just the sensor?
faq.a: Rarely — sensor is typically integral to the seat motor assembly.

title: Driver Seat Memory Module Circuit
shortDescription: Memory seat module communication or power fault.
fullDescription:
Code B0157 flags an internal or communication fault in the dedicated memory seat module (often mounted under the driver seat). It may fail to answer on the body LIN bus, or report an internal EEPROM error when trying to save a preset.

Power and ground to the module should be checked first — blown fuse, corroded ground strap on the seat frame, or water damage are common. If power is good but the module is unresponsive, it must be replaced and reprogrammed.

After replacement, memory positions must be re-taught.
safetyImpact: None — memory seat unavailable, manual operation preserved.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse and power
fixSteps.instruction: Verify seat module power and ground pins.

fixSteps.title: LIN scan
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool to ping module; check for no-response.

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: Install new module, program VIN, re-teach positions.

faq.q: Does a new module need programming?
faq.a: Yes — it must be coded to the vehicle VIN.

title: Odometer EEPROM Write Error
shortDescription: Instrument cluster cannot update odometer memory.
fullDescription:
Code B1600 (revised variant) indicates the instrument cluster module failed to write the latest odometer value to its EEPROM. On most modern clusters, the odometer is stored in non-volatile memory and updated every few seconds of driving.

Causes include a worn EEPROM chip (common on older clusters with high write-cycle counts), low supply voltage during a crank event, or a bad ground that causes voltage spikes during writes.

This code is legally sensitive — odometer tampering investigations may reference it. Never attempt to rewrite EEPROM manually.
safetyImpact: None directly — but odometer inaccuracy can affect service intervals and legal matters.

fixSteps.title: Test battery/charging
fixSteps.instruction: Verify healthy battery and alternator output.

fixSteps.title: Check ground
fixSteps.instruction: Locate cluster ground point on dash frame; clean.

fixSteps.title: Replace cluster
fixSteps.instruction: If EEPROM is failed, replace cluster and have mileage transferred at a licensed shop.

faq.q: Is DIY cluster swap legal?
faq.a: Mileage programming must be done per jurisdiction law — use a licensed shop.

title: Trip Meter Circuit Fault
shortDescription: Cluster cannot store or reset trip meter values.
fullDescription:
Code B1601 indicates the instrument cluster's trip meter memory (usually part of the same EEPROM as the odometer) is failing or the reset button circuit is stuck. The trip odometer may not advance, may reset randomly, or not respond to the reset press.

On some vehicles, a stuck reset stalk causes a continuous-input signal that sets this code. Check the stalk first — it's cheaper than a cluster.

If the stalk is fine, suspect the cluster board.
safetyImpact: None — cosmetic/convenience fault only.

fixSteps.title: Test stalk
fixSteps.instruction: Actuate reset button — listen/feel for proper click; check continuity.

fixSteps.title: Replace stalk
fixSteps.instruction: If stuck, replace turn-signal/stalk assembly.

fixSteps.title: Cluster check
fixSteps.instruction: If still faulting, send cluster for rebuild.

faq.q: Why does my trip randomly reset?
faq.a: Usually a stuck reset stalk triggering continuously.

title: VIN Mismatch Between Cluster and PCM
shortDescription: Cluster VIN does not match PCM VIN.
fullDescription:
Code B1602 is set when the instrument cluster and powertrain control module disagree on the vehicle's VIN. This occurs after a module swap (used cluster or used PCM from a donor vehicle) or an incomplete reprogramming session.

Anti-theft systems can latch hard when this code sets — the engine may go into immobilizer mode and refuse to start.

Resolution requires a factory scan tool or a skilled locksmith to rewrite the VIN in the appropriate module.
safetyImpact: May cause no-start due to immobilizer lockout.

fixSteps.title: Verify VINs
fixSteps.instruction: Read VIN from both cluster and PCM with scan tool; compare to dash VIN.

fixSteps.title: Program VIN
fixSteps.instruction: Use factory scan tool or locksmith service to rewrite matching VIN.

fixSteps.title: Verify no-start clears
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle ignition, confirm engine starts and codes clear.

faq.q: Can I fix this myself?
faq.a: Only with a factory-capable tool — most DIYers need a dealer or locksmith.

title: Front Left Speaker Circuit Open
shortDescription: Amplifier detected an open circuit on front-left speaker output.
fullDescription:
Code B1790 indicates the audio amplifier has detected no load (open circuit) on the front-left speaker output. Factory amps run a low-current pulse through each speaker when the head unit boots to detect presence.

Common causes are a blown speaker voice coil, a pinched wire in the door jamb (from opening/closing), or a disconnected head unit harness after aftermarket work.

Open-circuit codes sometimes trigger amp shutdown to protect the output stage.
safetyImpact: None — audio only.

causes.cause: Broken wire in door jamb boot

fixSteps.title: Swap-test speaker
fixSteps.instruction: Swap with a known-good speaker to confirm.

fixSteps.title: Inspect door boot
fixSteps.instruction: Flex door boot, check for broken speaker wires.

fixSteps.title: Repair
fixSteps.instruction: Solder/heat-shrink broken wires or replace speaker.

faq.q: Aftermarket speakers cause this?
faq.a: Yes if impedance is too high — factory amps expect 4Ω typically.

title: Front Right Speaker Circuit Short
shortDescription: Amplifier detected a short on front-right speaker output.
fullDescription:
Code B1797 indicates a short circuit across the front-right speaker output, either speaker-to-ground or across the + and - terminals. The amplifier will shut down that channel to protect itself.

Causes include a pinched wire in the door jamb shorted to the door frame, a shorted voice coil, or moisture on the speaker terminals from window leaks.

After repair, cycle key to reset amplifier protection.
safetyImpact: None — audio only.

causes.cause: Pinched wire shorting to door frame

fixSteps.title: Unplug speaker
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect speaker and recheck code to isolate wiring vs speaker.

fixSteps.title: Measure
fixSteps.instruction: With speaker unplugged, ohm check both wires to chassis.

fixSteps.title: Repair short
fixSteps.instruction: Relocate pinched wire or replace speaker.

faq.q: Amp damaged by short?
faq.a: Usually not — modern amps have protection, but repeated shorts shorten life.

title: External Amplifier Communication Lost
shortDescription: Head unit lost communication with external amplifier.
fullDescription:
Code B1842 is set when the head unit (or infotainment master) stops receiving messages from the external (trunk or kick-panel) amplifier over the MOST or audio CAN bus. Without the amp, system goes silent or reverts to stub speakers.

Causes include a blown amp fuse, water ingress in the trunk (very common on sedans with leaky trunk seals), or a corroded fiber connector on MOST systems.

On MOST-bus systems, every node must pass the optical signal — a single bad node can blind the whole ring.
safetyImpact: None — audio only.

fixSteps.title: Check amp fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Locate amp in trunk/kick panel; test fuse.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for water
fixSteps.instruction: Check amp mounting area for wetness and corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Clean MOST fiber
fixSteps.instruction: On MOST systems, unplug, clean fiber tip with lens wipe, reseat.

faq.q: Trunk leak cause?
faq.a: Yes — rain water running into trunk submerges many factory amps.

title: Amplifier Over-Temperature Shutdown
shortDescription: Amp thermal protection activated.
fullDescription:
Code B1858 records that the external amplifier entered thermal protection. Modern amps track internal temperature and shut down outputs above roughly 85°C (185°F) to prevent damage.

Causes include blocked amp ventilation (stuff piled on trunk amps), failed cooling fan (on amps so-equipped), or a shorted speaker output forcing high current.

After cooling, the amp resumes normal operation, but repeated thermal events indicate an underlying problem.
safetyImpact: None — amp self-protects.
symptoms: Audio cuts out when loud or hot

fixSteps.title: Clear amp area
fixSteps.instruction: Remove items blocking trunk amp ventilation.

fixSteps.title: Test fan
fixSteps.instruction: If amp has a fan, verify it spins with audio at high volume.

fixSteps.title: Check speakers
fixSteps.instruction: Diagnose any shorted speaker that might force high current.

faq.q: Is the amp damaged?
faq.a: Usually not — protection is designed to prevent damage.

title: Driver Window Motor Circuit
shortDescription: BCM detected fault in driver power window motor circuit.
fullDescription:
Code B1810 indicates the body control module has detected an out-of-range current or no response from the driver-side power window motor. The motor combines a Hall-effect pulse counter (for one-touch and anti-pinch) with a reversible DC motor.

Common causes are worn motor brushes (window moves slowly or stops), a failed Hall sensor (one-touch and anti-pinch stop working), or a frozen/damaged regulator forcing high current.

After motor replacement, anti-pinch calibration must be performed — usually by holding Up until stall, then Down until stall.
safetyImpact: Anti-pinch may be disabled; pinch risk during close.

fixSteps.title: Scan data
fixSteps.instruction: Observe motor current during operation with scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Test regulator
fixSteps.instruction: Remove door card, free regulator from motor, verify track is clean.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new regulator/motor assembly; relearn anti-pinch.

faq.q: Why relearn after swap?
faq.a: Module needs new pulse count reference to detect obstructions.

title: Passenger Window Switch Input Stuck
shortDescription: BCM detected passenger window switch input stuck active.
fullDescription:
Code B1815 is set when the passenger door window switch is reported active for longer than a sensible operation period — implying a stuck button or shorted wire. BCM will ignore the switch until the input normalizes, to prevent continuous motor operation.

Most common cause is spilled drinks under the switch cluster. Silicone spray cleaning sometimes works; otherwise replace the switch assembly.

Door card water intrusion from a failed moisture barrier also shorts switch wiring.
safetyImpact: Passenger window unusable from that switch.
symptoms: Window moves only from master switch

fixSteps.title: Clean switch
fixSteps.instruction: Remove switch, spray contact cleaner, cycle.

fixSteps.title: Inspect moisture barrier
fixSteps.instruction: Pop door card, verify plastic barrier is sealed.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Install new switch and test.

faq.q: Coca-Cola killed it?
faq.a: Sugar drinks are a frequent culprit — dries sticky.

title: Rear Window Lockout Switch Fault
shortDescription: Rear window lockout/child-lock switch signal inconsistent.
fullDescription:
Code B1820 indicates the master rear-window lockout switch — the child-safety button on the driver door that disables rear window controls — is giving an inconsistent signal. BCM sees it going on/off rapidly or stuck in one position.

Causes include a physically broken switch or a shorted wire in the master switch assembly. In rare cases the BCM itself has a failed input.

Until fixed, rear windows may default to disabled (safer) or enabled depending on the OEM strategy.
safetyImpact: Rear window control logic uncertain.

fixSteps.title: Cycle button
fixSteps.instruction: Press lockout multiple times, observe scan data.

fixSteps.title: Inspect switch
fixSteps.instruction: Remove master switch, check lockout contacts.

fixSteps.title: Replace assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Swap master switch panel.

faq.q: Is there a bypass?
faq.a: Not recommended — child safety is real.

title: Sunroof Motor Circuit Fault
shortDescription: Sunroof motor current out of range or no response.
fullDescription:
Code B1830 indicates the sunroof module has detected an out-of-range current on the sunroof motor, or lost its Hall pulse feedback. Sunroof motors include anti-pinch sensing to stop if blocked.

Causes include worn motor brushes, debris/leaves in the sunroof track (making the motor work harder), a slipping drive cable, or damaged Hall sensor inside the motor.

After motor or module repair, a full initialization (close-close-hold) is required to relearn endpoints.
safetyImpact: Anti-pinch may fail; pinch hazard.

fixSteps.title: Clean tracks
fixSteps.instruction: Open sunroof fully, vacuum debris, wipe tracks.

fixSteps.title: Lubricate
fixSteps.instruction: Apply white lithium grease to tracks and cable.

fixSteps.title: Initialize
fixSteps.instruction: Close switch held ~10s past close to reinitialize.

faq.q: How often clean tracks?
faq.a: Every 6-12 months if you park under trees.

title: Sunroof Position Not Learned
shortDescription: Sunroof module has no valid endpoint calibration.
fullDescription:
Code B1835 indicates the sunroof module has lost or never stored its open/closed endpoint reference. This commonly happens after a dead battery, module replacement, or motor swap.

Until initialized, the sunroof may only operate in short increments or not at all. Initialization procedure varies by make: typical is 'hold close switch for 10+ seconds past fully closed'.

If initialization fails repeatedly, the motor pulse sensor is suspect.
safetyImpact: Anti-pinch inactive until calibrated.
symptoms: Sunroof moves only while holding button

fixSteps.title: Initialization
fixSteps.instruction: Hold close button past full close for 10-15s.

fixSteps.title: Verify
fixSteps.instruction: Test one-touch operation.

fixSteps.title: Diagnose motor
fixSteps.instruction: If learn fails, test motor Hall sensor output.

faq.q: Why after battery change?
faq.a: Power loss clears RAM endpoints on some modules.

title: Fuel Door Release Solenoid Circuit
shortDescription: Fuel filler door release solenoid circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B1900 indicates the BCM has detected an open or short in the fuel door release solenoid — the small electric latch that pops the filler door when the driver presses the release button.

Common causes include a corroded connector at the solenoid (rear quarter panel), a broken wire near the hinge, or a failed solenoid. Some vehicles default to a manual release cable inside the trunk when the solenoid fails.

Repair is typically trim removal and solenoid replacement.
safetyImpact: None — convenience only.
symptoms: Fuel door won't open from button

fixSteps.title: Test button input
fixSteps.instruction: With scan tool, actuate solenoid while listening for click.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Access solenoid via trunk trim; check connector and wiring.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Install new solenoid and test.

faq.q: Emergency fuel access?
faq.a: Most cars have a manual release cable in the trunk — check owner manual.

title: Fuel Filler Door Ajar Sensor
shortDescription: Sensor detects fuel filler door ajar or signal implausible.
fullDescription:
Code B1901 indicates the fuel filler door ajar sensor (where equipped) is reporting an open or implausible signal. On capless-fill systems, this sensor interlocks with the EVAP system and may block refueling until the door is properly latched.

Causes include debris preventing full closure, a bent hinge, or a failed Hall/reed sensor. Some vehicles set this after a fuel cap/door collision repair.

Until resolved, some models refuse to unlock the capless flap.
safetyImpact: May block refueling until resolved.

fixSteps.title: Clear debris
fixSteps.instruction: Check door perimeter for leaves/ice.

fixSteps.title: Check hinge
fixSteps.instruction: Verify door closes flush; adjust hinge or striker.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If sensor failed, swap sensor or entire fuel door assembly.

faq.q: Can I still refuel?
faq.a: On some cars yes after the warning, others no until fixed.

title: Remote Start Request Circuit Fault
shortDescription: The remote start request signal to the BCM is faulty or out of range.
fullDescription:
Code B1400 indicates the body control module detected an implausible signal on the remote start request circuit. This typically comes from the key fob receiver module, dedicated remote start module, or factory telematics unit (OnStar, Uconnect, FordPass).

When triggered, the vehicle refuses to remote start or the engine may start and immediately shut off. Often sets after low battery events, module reprogramming, or aftermarket remote start installs that tap the wrong wires.
safetyImpact: No driving impact; remote convenience feature disabled.

fixSteps.title: Replace fob battery
fixSteps.instruction: Install fresh CR2032 and resync fob per owner's manual.

fixSteps.title: Scan module data
fixSteps.instruction: Check BCM remote start input state while pressing the fob.

fixSteps.title: Inspect aftermarket wiring
fixSteps.instruction: If a 3rd-party remote start is installed, verify tach, brake, and neutral-safety splices.

faq.q: Why does my engine start then die?
faq.a: The immobilizer isn't recognizing the remote start permission — often a fob or BCM programming issue.

title: Remote Start Disable Request Active
shortDescription: The system received a valid disable signal preventing remote start operation.
fullDescription:
B1401 means the BCM has active conditions blocking remote start: hood open, key-in-ignition, alarm tripped, or previous stall event. Not always a fault — often a status code that needs clearing once conditions are corrected.

Common on GM, Ford, and Ram trucks after hood cable adjustments or when the hood ajar switch sticks. Also sets if remote start is attempted more than the allowed retries (usually 2) without the driver entering the vehicle.
safetyImpact: No safety impact.

fixSteps.title: Cycle the hood
fixSteps.instruction: Fully open and slam the hood closed.

fixSteps.title: Read BCM status
fixSteps.instruction: Check hood switch input live data.

fixSteps.title: Replace hood switch
fixSteps.instruction: If stuck open in software, replace the switch.

faq.q: Is this a real failure?
faq.a: Usually just a status — correct the condition (close hood, remove key) and retry.

title: Key Fob Antenna / Receiver Fault
shortDescription: The remote keyless entry antenna or receiver module circuit failed.
fullDescription:
Code B1403 is logged when the BCM or dedicated RKE (Remote Keyless Entry) receiver loses communication with its antenna or reports low RF signal strength. Antennas are usually mounted in the rear glass, headliner, or rear bumper cover.

Symptoms include fobs working only within 1-2 feet of the car, intermittent door lock response, and passive entry (touch-to-unlock handles) failing randomly.
safetyImpact: Reduced convenience; mechanical key entry still works.

fixSteps.title: Remove interferers
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug aftermarket USB chargers and LED ballasts, retest.

fixSteps.title: Inspect antenna connector
fixSteps.instruction: Locate RKE receiver (often under rear deck or in headliner) and reseat coax.

fixSteps.title: Replace receiver
fixSteps.instruction: Swap RKE module; may need programming.

faq.q: Do I need dealer programming?
faq.a: Usually yes for receiver replacement; some aftermarket modules learn fobs themselves.

title: Key Fob Not Programmed / Unrecognized
shortDescription: The BCM received a transmission from a fob ID not in its authorized list.
fullDescription:
B1407 appears after a fob replacement, battery change on some systems, or when a stranger's fob transmits nearby. Also seen after BCM replacement before fobs are learned.

The vehicle will not remote start or respond to fob buttons until the fob is properly programmed. Most manufacturers require the dealer scan tool or a capable bidirectional aftermarket scanner to add fobs.
safetyImpact: Keyless features disabled; ignition key still works mechanically.

causes.cause: Fob ID lost after BCM reset

symptoms: Multiple fob batteries changed at once

fixSteps.title: Reprogram fobs
fixSteps.instruction: Follow make-specific procedure or use bidirectional scanner.

fixSteps.title: Purchase OEM fob
fixSteps.instruction: Avoid cheap clones which often fail to learn.

fixSteps.title: Dealer re-flash BCM
fixSteps.instruction: If all fobs were erased, security reset may be required.

faq.q: Why can't I program it myself?
faq.a: Manufacturer security protocols lock fob learning to authenticated tools on most post-2010 vehicles.

title: Remote Start Relay Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: The remote start relay control or feedback circuit is open/shorted.
fullDescription:
B1410 indicates the BCM commanded the remote start relay and either got no feedback or the wrong state back. The relay feeds the starter solenoid, fuel pump, or ignition line depending on design.

Common on factory remote start systems after winter — corrosion in the relay socket or under-hood fuse box is a frequent cause. On aftermarket installs, a stuck relay is often due to a failed diode in the kit.
safetyImpact: May cause no-start or continuous cranking if relay sticks.
symptoms: Remote start clicks but no crank

fixSteps.title: Swap relay
fixSteps.instruction: Substitute with identical relay from horn or fog lamp circuit to isolate.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect remote start fuse in underhood box.

fixSteps.title: Test BCM output
fixSteps.instruction: Back-probe relay control wire while commanding start.

faq.q: Can a bad relay damage the starter?
faq.a: Yes — a stuck relay can over-crank and burn the starter motor.

title: Passive Entry Door Handle Sensor Fault
shortDescription: One or more door handle capacitive touch sensors report invalid data.
fullDescription:
B1425 is set when the 'keyless go' or 'smart entry' door handle sensor circuit fails. Each door handle has a capacitive or button sensor that wakes the system when the fob is in range and the driver touches the handle.

Common failure after car washes, pothole jolts, or handle paint repairs. Water migrates into the sensor body and causes intermittent triggers or permanent opens.
safetyImpact: Must use fob button to unlock; no driving impact.

causes.cause: Broken sensor wire at door hinge

fixSteps.title: Flex door boot wire
fixSteps.instruction: Check wire harness at hinge for breaks, common wear point.

fixSteps.title: Dry out handle
fixSteps.instruction: Remove handle and air-dry 24 hours; reseal with silicone.

fixSteps.title: Replace handle
fixSteps.instruction: Swap complete handle assembly with sensor.

faq.q: Why only after car wash?
faq.a: High-pressure sprays push water past the handle seal into the sensor.

title: Brake Pedal Input Required for Start
shortDescription: Push-button start requires brake depression signal that was not detected.
fullDescription:
B1428 logs when the driver pressed Start without sufficient brake pedal input, OR when the brake pedal switch circuit has failed so the BCM never sees the input. Also sets during aborted remote start when brake was pressed (remote start auto-aborts if brake is touched before driver enters).

For diagnostic purposes, pair with any C-codes referencing brake switch to distinguish operator error from switch failure.
safetyImpact: Vehicle won't start until brake signal restored.

fixSteps.title: Check brake lights
fixSteps.instruction: If all brake lights dead, suspect switch or fuse.

fixSteps.title: Replace brake switch
fixSteps.instruction: Located at pedal bracket; adjust plunger preload.

fixSteps.title: Clear code and retest
fixSteps.instruction: Press brake firmly and push start.

faq.q: Why are my brake lights off?
faq.a: The same switch controls both brake lights and start enable.

title: Anti-theft System Indicator Circuit
shortDescription: The security indicator lamp circuit is open or shorted.
fullDescription:
B1440 means the BCM cannot verify the state of the anti-theft (security) indicator LED. This bulb/LED blinks when the vehicle is armed and steady when an anti-theft event is active.

Though the indicator itself is minor, the code often blocks the immobilizer self-test and may prevent remote start or keyless crank until cleared.
safetyImpact: Security status not visible; system usually still functional.

fixSteps.title: Test LED circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Read BCM indicator output in live data.

fixSteps.title: Replace cluster bulb/LED
fixSteps.instruction: Often requires instrument cluster removal.

fixSteps.title: Update BCM
fixSteps.instruction: Some TSBs address false B1440 sets.

faq.q: Is my car still secure?
faq.a: Yes, but you can't visually confirm arming state.

title: Passlock Sensor Data Invalid (GM)
shortDescription: The Passlock sensor in the lock cylinder sent an invalid code.
fullDescription:
B1441 is the classic GM Passlock fault — the lock cylinder contains a resistor/Hall sensor that must match when the key is turned. A worn tumbler or bad sensor causes the PCM to starve fuel for 10 minutes.

Well-known failure on 1998-2007 GM trucks, Impala, Malibu, and Cavalier. Symptom: car cranks, starts for 2 seconds, then dies with SECURITY light solid.
safetyImpact: Vehicle won't run until 10-minute relearn completes.

fixSteps.title: Perform 10-min relearn
fixSteps.instruction: Turn key to ON, wait 10 min with Security light out, then crank.

fixSteps.title: Replace Passlock sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Drill-out or replace lock cylinder assembly.

fixSteps.title: Bypass module install
fixSteps.instruction: Aftermarket Passlock bypass available for persistent failures.

faq.q: Can I bypass Passlock?
faq.a: Yes with an aftermarket module; insurance implications vary by region.

title: Immobilizer Control Module Fault
shortDescription: The transponder / immobilizer control module failed self-test.
fullDescription:
B1442 indicates the immobilizer module (sometimes called WCM, SKREEM, or EIS depending on make) failed internal diagnostics. The module reads the transponder chip in your key and tells the PCM whether to allow fuel.

Often destroyed by water (floor leaks), jump-start surges, or reverse battery connection. Replacement typically requires proprietary programming with matching key data.
safetyImpact: Vehicle will not start; requires professional diagnosis.

fixSteps.title: Confirm with scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Read all modules; immobilizer may be offline on CAN.

fixSteps.title: Check module for water
fixSteps.instruction: Many immobilizers mount low on dash or under steering column.

fixSteps.title: Replace and program
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer or locksmith with OEM tool required.

faq.q: Can a locksmith do this cheaper than dealer?
faq.a: Often yes — automotive locksmiths with OEM tools are 30-50% cheaper.

title: Transponder Key ID Mismatch
shortDescription: The key's transponder ID does not match any stored ID in the immobilizer.
fullDescription:
B1445 sets when a key is inserted and cranked but its RFID transponder either sends no code or a code not in memory. Happens after module replacement, cloned key installation, or when an unprogrammed spare is used.

Differentiate from B1407 (RKE fob) — B1445 is specifically the transponder chip that permits fuel/spark, not the remote buttons.
safetyImpact: Vehicle will not start with this key.

fixSteps.title: Try known-good key
fixSteps.instruction: If spare works, issue is isolated to the suspect key.

fixSteps.title: Program suspect key
fixSteps.instruction: Follow make-specific programming; may need dealer tool.

fixSteps.title: Replace transponder
fixSteps.instruction: Have locksmith cut and program new OEM key.

faq.q: Why did my working key suddenly fail?
faq.a: Transponders can fail after magnetic exposure or physical damage to the key head.

title: Immobilizer Antenna Ring Circuit Fault
shortDescription: The ring antenna around the ignition cylinder has an open or short.
fullDescription:
B1447 points to the pickup coil (antenna ring) that reads the transponder in the key head. It's a small ring around the ignition lock cylinder connected by a short harness to the immobilizer.

Failure modes: the antenna wire breaks from repeated key turns, or the connector backs out. A no-start where the immobilizer says 'key not detected' even with a known-good key points here.
safetyImpact: Vehicle will not start.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Remove steering column cover and reseat antenna plug.

fixSteps.title: Resistance test
fixSteps.instruction: Measure antenna coil resistance per service manual.

fixSteps.title: Replace antenna ring
fixSteps.instruction: Part is usually sold separately from lock cylinder.

faq.q: Is this the same as Passlock?
faq.a: No — Passlock reads key position, this reads the chip RFID.

title: Alarm Siren Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: The anti-theft alarm siren output or feedback circuit is faulty.
fullDescription:
B1449 fires when the BCM detects an open, short, or incorrect current draw on the alarm siren control line. Most factory sirens have a tamper-detect battery that also reports to the BCM; a dead siren backup battery commonly sets this code.

Often seen with vehicles 8+ years old when the siren's internal backup battery dies. The alarm may still chirp on lock/unlock but won't sound if the car battery is disconnected during a theft attempt.
safetyImpact: Alarm reduced effectiveness; vehicle still operates normally.

fixSteps.title: Locate siren
fixSteps.instruction: Usually in fender liner or under hood near battery.

fixSteps.title: Replace siren
fixSteps.instruction: Complete unit — backup battery is not serviceable.

fixSteps.title: Program new siren
fixSteps.instruction: Some makes require BCM to learn new siren.

faq.q: Does this void theft insurance?
faq.a: Possibly — check your policy; inoperative alarm is often a disclosure item.

title: PCM-BCM Authentication Failure
shortDescription: The PCM and BCM failed to exchange the rolling authentication code.
fullDescription:
B1450 is the deepest security fault — the PCM and BCM use a rolling code over CAN/SCP to verify each other. If the codes don't match, the PCM cuts fuel and the BCM logs B1450.

Causes: a replaced PCM or BCM that wasn't paired, a CAN bus fault causing messages to drop, or an intrusion attempt. After any PCM or BCM swap, a pairing procedure (often with VIN write) must be performed.
safetyImpact: Vehicle will not start until modules are re-paired.

fixSteps.title: Read all codes
fixSteps.instruction: Check for companion U0100/U0140 U-codes.

fixSteps.title: Pair modules
fixSteps.instruction: Use factory or equivalent tool to perform BCM/PCM marriage.

fixSteps.title: Inspect CAN wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Resistance 60 ohm across CAN-H to CAN-L at OBD port.

faq.q: Why does my used junkyard PCM cause this?
faq.a: The VIN/security seed doesn't match your BCM — must be re-flashed.

title: Power Liftgate Motor Circuit Open
shortDescription: The power liftgate lift motor circuit shows no current when commanded.
fullDescription:
B1750 means the hatch/liftgate control module commanded motor movement but sensed no current flow. Common on Ford Explorer, Escape, Chrysler Pacifica, Honda Odyssey, and most Asian crossovers with power liftgates.

Motors live in the D-pillars and hinge area where flexing wire bundles fatigue over years. A break in the flex loom is the #1 cause on vehicles older than 7 years.
safetyImpact: Manual liftgate operation still possible.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Under-dash or rear fuse panel, labeled POWER LIFTGATE.

fixSteps.title: Inspect hinge loom
fixSteps.instruction: Peel back rubber boot at roof hinge, flex wires while scanning.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor strut
fixSteps.instruction: Swap one or both powered struts.

faq.q: Do I have to replace both struts?
faq.a: Good practice — same age means second failure is near.

title: Power Liftgate Obstruction Detected
shortDescription: The liftgate reversed direction due to sensed obstruction.
fullDescription:
B1751 is a protective event — the module detected a current spike or pinch-strip trigger and reversed motion. Not necessarily a fault, but if logged repeatedly with no actual obstruction, the pinch sensor or position sensor is drifting.

Common after winter — ice or frozen seals cause real obstructions. Also triggered by roof racks or loaded cargo boxes impeding travel.
safetyImpact: Safety feature working as designed unless false triggers.

fixSteps.title: Clear obstructions
fixSteps.instruction: Remove ice, snow, check trim alignment.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate liftgate
fixSteps.instruction: Most makes have a travel relearn — manually move fully open/closed.

fixSteps.title: Inspect pinch strip
fixSteps.instruction: Rubber strip along gate edge; cracks cause false trips.

faq.q: Why does it trigger with nothing in the way?
faq.a: Temperature drops change strut resistance, which looks like obstruction.

title: Liftgate Latch Assembly Malfunction
shortDescription: The power latch (cinching or release) on the liftgate failed.
fullDescription:
B1752 targets the electric latch that cinches the liftgate closed in the final inch of travel, or the electric release that unlocks it. Common on Lincoln, Cadillac, Mercedes, and luxury SUVs with soft-close rear hatches.

Latch motors burn out when forced by manual closing over many years, or when the seal swells causing high resistance.
safetyImpact: Gate may not latch fully or require manual slam.

fixSteps.title: Adjust striker
fixSteps.instruction: Loosen bolts and shift striker for better engagement.

fixSteps.title: Replace latch
fixSteps.instruction: Complete latch assembly including motor.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle gate through full travel after replacement.

faq.q: Can I still use the manual latch?
faq.a: Usually yes via emergency cable inside the gate.

title: Hatch Motor Overcurrent
shortDescription: The liftgate motor drew excessive current during operation.
fullDescription:
B1753 is logged when motor amperage exceeds the module's threshold. Cause is typically binding: weak gas struts forcing the motor to do all the work, damaged ball sockets, or frozen hinges.

Ignoring this code eventually burns out the motor, turning a $40 gas strut job into a $600 motor replacement.
safetyImpact: Motor life shortened; eventual failure expected.

fixSteps.title: Replace gas struts
fixSteps.instruction: Support gate and swap both struts.

fixSteps.title: Lubricate hinges
fixSteps.instruction: Spray hinge pins and ball sockets with synthetic grease.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: If already damaged, full strut+motor swap.

faq.q: How do I know which strut is weak?
faq.a: If gate sags when open, or falls when unassisted, struts are gone.

title: Sliding Door Motor Circuit Fault
shortDescription: The power sliding door (minivan) motor circuit is open or shorted.
fullDescription:
B1760 fires on minivans like Honda Odyssey, Toyota Sienna, Chrysler Pacifica, Kia Carnival — the power sliding door won't operate. The door has 3-4 motors (latch, cinch, main travel, and sometimes power release).

Most common cause is the main track motor after kids slam the door open/closed. Also check the upper-center cable which frays and binds.
safetyImpact: Manual operation usually still works.

fixSteps.title: Inspect center track
fixSteps.instruction: Look for dents and dry-lubed cable.

fixSteps.title: Lubricate tracks
fixSteps.instruction: Silicone-safe grease on all three tracks.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor/cable
fixSteps.instruction: Cassette is one unit on most vans.

faq.q: My kids slam it — is that why it broke?
faq.a: Yes — always use the button or handle gently; slamming strips the plastic gears.

title: Tailgate Position Sensor Out of Range
shortDescription: The Hall-effect position sensor reports invalid angle.
fullDescription:
B1770 indicates the liftgate angle sensor reported a value outside plausible range. The sensor allows the module to halt at the last-memorized open height (useful for garages).

Sensor sits at the hinge and gets moisture over time. When it fails, the gate may travel too far, hit the roof, or fail to close.
safetyImpact: Risk of gate hitting garage ceiling if set-height feature used.

fixSteps.title: Clean connector
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat hinge sensor plug with dielectric grease.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Part of the hinge assembly on some vehicles.

fixSteps.title: Recalibrate memory
fixSteps.instruction: Re-teach open position via button combo.

faq.q: Why does it hit my garage ceiling?
faq.a: The memory-height feature relies on this sensor.

title: Soft-Close Cinch Motor Fault
shortDescription: The soft-close (final cinching) motor failed to complete its cycle.
fullDescription:
B1780 targets the secondary cinch motor that pulls the door or liftgate from the first detent to fully closed. Common on luxury cars (BMW, Mercedes, Lexus, Lincoln) that have 'soft close' doors.

Cinch motors run for 2-3 seconds per close; with hundreds of uses per year they eventually wear. A good indicator is hearing the motor whir without the door actually pulling in.
safetyImpact: Door can be closed manually with firmer slam.

fixSteps.title: Thaw and retry
fixSteps.instruction: If freezing temps, warm car and retest.

fixSteps.title: Replace cinch motor
fixSteps.instruction: Latch assembly replacement typically.

fixSteps.title: Program replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Some systems need cinch learn routine.

faq.q: Is soft-close worth fixing?
faq.a: Functionally no, but resale value drops significantly without it.

title: Active Headrest Actuator Fault - Driver
shortDescription: The driver active headrest mechanism failed its self-test.
fullDescription:
B1900 on Toyota, Mercedes, Saab, and Volvo with Active Head Restraints (AHR) means the spring-loaded or pyrotechnic device in the headrest failed readiness. AHRs deploy forward during rear impacts to reduce whiplash.

Known issue on 2005-2010 Mercedes where the plastic cam weakens and the headrest fires during normal use — a recall covers some VINs.
safetyImpact: Reduced whiplash protection in rear collisions.

fixSteps.title: Inspect headrest
fixSteps.instruction: Look for partial deployment or broken plastic visible.

fixSteps.title: Replace headrest
fixSteps.instruction: Entire unit — pyro version requires qualified tech.

fixSteps.title: Check TSBs/recalls
fixSteps.instruction: Verify your VIN against open recalls.

faq.q: Can I drive with this code?
faq.a: Yes but whiplash protection is compromised; rear-collision risk.

title: Active Headrest Actuator Fault - Passenger
shortDescription: The front passenger active headrest mechanism failed self-test.
fullDescription:
B1901 is the passenger-side equivalent of B1900. Same mechanism, same failure modes. Diagnose by swapping driver and passenger headrests if mechanically compatible — code follows the hardware.

Mercedes owners: check Campaign 2008030012 if affected.
safetyImpact: Reduced passenger whiplash protection.

fixSteps.title: Swap L/R headrests
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm code moves with the unit.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed headrest
fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM part; aftermarket often lacks squib.

fixSteps.title: Clear SRS codes
fixSteps.instruction: Requires SRS-capable scanner.

faq.q: Do I need a dealer?
faq.a: Pyrotechnic versions usually yes; spring versions DIY-friendly.

title: Active Headrest Stored (Post-Deploy)
shortDescription: An active headrest has deployed and must be reset or replaced.
fullDescription:
B1905 is a historic code set after deployment. On spring-type (Saab, Volvo) a release button on the seatback manually resets it. On pyrotechnic systems (Mercedes), the headrest is one-time-use and must be replaced.

Common after rear-end collisions — even minor ones can deploy AHR. Verify vehicle history before buying a used car with this code.
safetyImpact: No further protection on deployed side.

fixSteps.title: Identify system type
fixSteps.instruction: Spring vs pyro — check owner's manual.

fixSteps.title: Reset spring type
fixSteps.instruction: Push headrest back until it clicks with button held.

fixSteps.title: Replace pyro type
fixSteps.instruction: OEM headrest and programming required.

faq.q: Does my insurance cover this?
faq.a: After a collision claim, yes — often overlooked by body shops.

title: Trailer Connector Open Circuit
shortDescription: The trailer 7-pin or 4-pin connector reports no trailer present when expected.
fullDescription:
B2200 sets when the tow-package control module expects a trailer (e.g., gear selector shows Tow mode, or user enabled trailer) but sees no load. Usually set after aftermarket hitch install with an improper harness.

Integrated trailer brake controllers also require the connector to pass self-test on start-up. Most common cause: corrosion on the brake pin (blue) causing open circuit.
safetyImpact: Trailer brakes and lights may be inoperative.

fixSteps.title: Clean connector
fixSteps.instruction: Brass brush both trailer and vehicle side; apply dielectric grease.

fixSteps.title: Test at pins
fixSteps.instruction: Ground, left/right turn, tail, brake, and trailer brake.

fixSteps.title: Inspect T-connector
fixSteps.instruction: On aftermarket wiring, replace T-connector harness.

faq.q: Do I need factory tow package?
faq.a: No, but integrated trailer brake requires it or a high-quality aftermarket controller.

title: Trailer Brake Controller Output Fault
shortDescription: The integrated trailer brake controller output circuit is faulty.
fullDescription:
B2205 specifically targets the controller side — the PWM signal to the trailer brakes is open or shorted. Unlike B2200 which is the connector, this is upstream in the cab controller.

Ford, Ram, Chevy HD trucks all have ITBCs from the factory. Shorts happen when trailers are plugged in with wet/damaged plugs, spiking current back to the controller and blowing its internal fuse.
safetyImpact: No trailer brake assistance — significantly increases stopping distance.
symptoms: Trailer brake icon with red X

fixSteps.title: Check in-line fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Behind dash panel near ITBC module.

fixSteps.title: Scan for shorts
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug trailer, reset code, see if returns.

fixSteps.title: Replace ITBC module
fixSteps.instruction: Integrated unit — programming may be required.

faq.q: Can I still tow?
faq.a: Small trailers without brakes yes; with electric brakes, no — unsafe.

title: Ambient Lighting Bus Communication Lost
shortDescription: The LIN or CAN communication to ambient lighting nodes is interrupted.
fullDescription:
B2300 on VW, Audi, BMW, Mercedes, Volvo — the multi-color ambient LED strips communicate via LIN bus from a master node (usually BCM or dedicated ambient controller). When one node drops off, the entire chain may go dark.

Common after interior service where trim was removed and a connector was missed. Also happens when one LED strip shorts and pulls the bus down.
safetyImpact: Aesthetic only; no driving impact.

fixSteps.title: Inspect recent work area
fixSteps.instruction: Check last disassembled trim for loose plug.

fixSteps.title: Isolate nodes
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect one LED zone at a time to find short.

fixSteps.title: Replace faulty strip
fixSteps.instruction: Individual LED strips are repairable.

faq.q: Is this a common issue?
faq.a: Yes on VAG cars after dash removal for AC or radio work.

title: Ambient Lighting Driver Short to Ground
shortDescription: One of the ambient LED drivers is shorted to ground.
fullDescription:
B2301 is set when the BCM detects its LED driver output pulled low with no command. Short to ground in the wiring or inside an LED module. The BCM protects itself by disabling that channel.

Often caused by pinched wires in door jambs or footwell trim. Occasionally an LED module fails internally.
safetyImpact: Affected zone dark; rest of ambient lighting may still work.

fixSteps.title: Remove trim
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect wire path for pinch points.

fixSteps.title: Unplug LED
fixSteps.instruction: If code clears, the LED unit is the short.

fixSteps.title: Replace LED strip
fixSteps.instruction: Match color depth (RGB vs RGBW).

faq.q: Can I use aftermarket LEDs?
faq.a: Yes but they may not speak the LIN protocol for color sync.

title: Ambient Light Sensor Out of Range
shortDescription: The exterior/cabin light sensor reports implausible values.
fullDescription:
B2302 relates to the photocell that dims interior ambient lighting at night. When it reports max/min continuously, the BCM disables auto-dimming and logs the fault.

Sensor is usually at the base of the windshield. Covered by a sticker, toll tag, or dashcam mount is the #1 cause of false high reads.
safetyImpact: Ambient lights stuck at fixed brightness.
symptoms: Dash stays dim or bright regardless of time

fixSteps.title: Clear sensor surface
fixSteps.instruction: Remove stickers, toll transponders in the area.

fixSteps.title: Cover/uncover test
fixSteps.instruction: Watch BCM data while shading sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Usually part of a rain/light combo sensor.

faq.q: Why do my headlights behave weirdly too?
faq.a: Same sensor controls auto-headlights on most cars.

title: Heated Seat Element Open - General
shortDescription: A seat heating element circuit is open.
fullDescription:
B2400 is a generic heated-seat element open code. The resistance wire in the cushion or backrest has broken, usually from cycling (expansion/contraction) or passenger wear over the bolster.

Once broken, the affected pad will not warm. Repair options: replace the element (cushion heater is ~$80, backrest heater ~$100) or use a universal aftermarket heat pad kit.
safetyImpact: Comfort feature only; no safety impact.
symptoms: Seat heat button toggles then turns off

fixSteps.title: Check connector
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and reseat harness under seat.

fixSteps.title: Measure element resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Should be 1-3 ohms depending on zone.

fixSteps.title: Replace heating element
fixSteps.instruction: Pad swap requires upholstery R&R.

faq.q: Is this safe to ignore?
faq.a: Yes, but humidity can short a damaged pad — potential fire risk in rare cases.

title: Heated Seat Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The seat thermistor reports out-of-range temperature.
fullDescription:
B2401 indicates the NTC thermistor embedded in the seat reports a value outside the module's plausibility window. The module uses it to prevent over-heating and adjust output.

When thermistor fails open, module disables heat as a safety measure. When shorted, it may cause the seat to run too hot.
safetyImpact: Potential for seat to overheat if sensor shorts low.

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance at module connector; should change with seat temp.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Often integrated into the heating pad itself.

fixSteps.title: Module calibration
fixSteps.instruction: Some systems need relearn after replacement.

faq.q: Should I just keep using it?
faq.a: If it runs too hot it can burn the upholstery; disable heat until fixed.

title: Driver Heated Seat Circuit Overload
shortDescription: The driver's seat heater drew excessive current.
fullDescription:
B2402 is seat-specific (driver) and indicates current draw above threshold. Typically a partial short from worn insulation at the seat belt pivot point or under the lumbar frame.

If left unrepaired, the wire can short harder and blow the seat fuse, which also kills the seat memory module on some vehicles.
safetyImpact: Fire risk if short becomes complete; disable use.

fixSteps.title: Disable seat heat
fixSteps.instruction: Remove fuse until repair complete.

fixSteps.title: Inspect under-seat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Pull seat, trace wires for rub marks.

fixSteps.title: Replace element or harness
fixSteps.instruction: Repair specific chafed wire or full pad swap.

faq.q: Is a burning smell normal?
faq.a: No — stop using immediately, this indicates an active short.

title: Passenger Heated Seat Element Open
shortDescription: The front passenger heated-seat element has an open circuit.
fullDescription:
B2410 mirrors B2400 but for the passenger seat. Failures on the passenger side are less common due to lower use, but occupant weight/detection wiring runs through the same harness — a harness failure can log both B2410 and airbag-related codes.

Diagnose harness continuity before assuming element failure.
safetyImpact: Passenger comfort only.

fixSteps.title: Test at module
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm output command vs no current flow.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check at seat slide track — common break point.

fixSteps.title: Replace element
fixSteps.instruction: Pad R&R via upholstery removal.

faq.q: Do I need to remove the airbag?
faq.a: Side airbag is integrated on most seats — dealer-level precautions required.

title: Ventilated Seat Fan Motor Fault
shortDescription: The cooled-seat (ventilated) fan motor is not responding.
fullDescription:
B2411 applies to ventilated seat systems (Cadillac, Lincoln, Mercedes, Lexus, BMW, Volvo). Small fans in the cushion and backrest draw cabin air through perforated leather. Fans fail from debris ingestion or bearing wear.

Average fan life is 80-120k miles. Pet hair accelerates failure. Replacement requires pulling the seat bottom or back skin.
safetyImpact: Seat cooling inoperative.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum seat perforations
fixSteps.instruction: Use crevice tool on seat surface.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan module
fixSteps.instruction: Access via underside of seat in most cases.

fixSteps.title: Verify module command
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm fan PWM output at connector.

faq.q: Why doesn't it feel cold?
faq.a: Ventilated seats blow cabin air — they don't actively chill, just evaporate sweat.

title: Rear Heated Seat Circuit Fault
shortDescription: Rear outboard heated seat element or control circuit failed.
fullDescription:
B2420 targets rear seat heating, common on luxury sedans and SUVs. Rear seats often share a single controller that switches between left/right outboard positions. When one side fails, the other may still work.

Wires routing under the carpet from front to rear are common break points, especially at the B-pillar transition.
safetyImpact: Rear passenger comfort only.

fixSteps.title: Test at rear seat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm 12V at command.

fixSteps.title: Pull rear seat
fixSteps.instruction: Access pad and harness.

fixSteps.title: Replace element
fixSteps.instruction: Universal replacement pads available.

faq.q: Is rear seat heat standard?
faq.a: Only on luxury trims; often an option package.

title: Heated Steering Wheel Element Open
shortDescription: The steering wheel heating element circuit is open.
fullDescription:
B2440 sets when the resistance wire in the wheel rim breaks. Failure usually happens at the 9 or 3 o'clock positions where drivers grip hardest. Some wheels use multiple zones; one zone can fail while others work.

Repair requires removing the wheel (airbag) and splicing the element or replacing the whole wheel assembly. Costly due to airbag handling.
safetyImpact: Comfort feature only.
symptoms: Heated wheel button flashes and turns off

fixSteps.title: Inspect switch
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm button commands heat function.

fixSteps.title: Test at clockspring
fixSteps.instruction: Measure element resistance through column.

fixSteps.title: Replace wheel
fixSteps.instruction: Requires airbag R&R — dealer recommended.

faq.q: Can I just replace the wire?
faq.a: Technically yes but wheel R&R is not DIY-safe due to the airbag.

title: Heated Steering Wheel Temperature Sensor
shortDescription: Steering wheel heater thermistor reports out of range.
fullDescription:
B2441 is the steering wheel version of B2401. The NTC embedded in the rim monitors heat to prevent burning the driver. Open/shorted sensor disables heating.

Paired with B2440 if both element and sensor fail — often happens together as both run in the same wire bundle through the clockspring.
safetyImpact: Wheel heat disabled.

fixSteps.title: Check clockspring continuity
fixSteps.instruction: Rotate wheel through full travel while measuring.

fixSteps.title: Replace clockspring
fixSteps.instruction: If broken internally, replacement needed.

fixSteps.title: Replace wheel if element faulted
fixSteps.instruction: Integrated repair.

faq.q: Why do I have airbag code too?
faq.a: Clockspring carries both the heater and airbag squib wires.

title: Inside Mirror Auto-Dim Circuit Fault
shortDescription: The inside rearview mirror auto-dim circuit is open or shorted.
fullDescription:
B2500 refers to the electrochromic inside mirror that darkens to reduce headlight glare. It uses two sensors (front for ambient, rear for glare) and a gel layer with voltage applied to change opacity.

Common failure: gel leaks from the mirror creating 'rainbow' discoloration, or the rear-facing sensor gets taped over by a dashcam mount.
safetyImpact: Mirror remains clear but won't dim — driver experiences glare.

fixSteps.title: Unobstruct sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove dashcam tape or stickers at rear of mirror.

fixSteps.title: Test voltages
fixSteps.instruction: With headlights behind, mirror should show ~1.2V across gel.

fixSteps.title: Replace mirror
fixSteps.instruction: Full assembly; some have homelink/camera that must transfer.

faq.q: Can I repair the gel?
faq.a: No — sealed unit, replace the whole mirror.

title: Outside Mirror Auto-Dim Fault
shortDescription: Exterior auto-dim mirror element has failed.
fullDescription:
B2501 applies to side mirrors that dim along with the inside mirror (slaved to the inside mirror signal). The exterior mirror has its own element but shares the dim command.

Typical failure: mirror heater shorts into the auto-dim element, damaging both. If mirror heater is DIY-replaced, verify element still functions.
safetyImpact: Side mirror glare at night.

fixSteps.title: Check slave wire
fixSteps.instruction: Inside mirror commands outside via dedicated wire.

fixSteps.title: Replace mirror glass
fixSteps.instruction: Glass comes as assembly with element.

fixSteps.title: Test after replace
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm dimming tracks inside mirror.

faq.q: Why does mirror heat matter?
faq.a: Shared ground — a bad heater often takes out the dim element.

title: Paddle Shifter Switch Fault
shortDescription: A steering wheel paddle shifter switch circuit is stuck or open.
fullDescription:
B2700 logs when the TCM or BCM sees an implausible signal from a paddle — either continuously pressed (stuck) or no response when commanded.

Most paddles are simple momentary switches routed through the clockspring. A stuck paddle may cause the trans to shift down on its own, which is a medium safety concern.
safetyImpact: Unexpected downshifts could cause loss of traction.

fixSteps.title: Watch live data
fixSteps.instruction: In neutral, press each paddle while watching scanner.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect paddles
fixSteps.instruction: If code clears, replace switch assembly.

fixSteps.title: Check clockspring
fixSteps.instruction: Verify continuity through full wheel rotation.

faq.q: Why does the car downshift on its own?
faq.a: A stuck paddle sends continuous downshift request.

title: Tiptronic Gate Position Sensor
shortDescription: The manual-mode gate position sensor in the shifter is faulty.
fullDescription:
B2701 refers to the +/- gate of a Tiptronic-style shifter. When in manual mode, bumping the lever left/right commands shifts; the sensor reports position to the TCM.

Common wear item on VW/Audi/Porsche with Tiptronic after 100k miles. Symptom: manual mode engages but shifts don't occur, or commands are delayed.
safetyImpact: Manual shifting unreliable; auto mode normally unaffected.

causes.cause: Connector loose at base of console

symptoms: Shifter light shows gear but no shift

fixSteps.title: Reseat shifter connector
fixSteps.instruction: Below console trim near shifter base.

fixSteps.title: Replace shifter assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Complete unit on most vehicles.

fixSteps.title: Program new shifter
fixSteps.instruction: Some require adaptation routine.

faq.q: Why only in manual mode?
faq.a: Auto mode uses the PRNDL sensor, not the gate sensor.

title: BCM RAM Memory Failure
shortDescription: BCM has detected a RAM read/write failure during self-test.
fullDescription:
Code B1002 indicates the Body Control Module has detected a fault in its random-access memory. The module performs power-on self-tests; if RAM cannot be written/read reliably, this code sets. The fault is typically permanent and requires module replacement.

Before replacing, confirm stable battery voltage and clean grounds, as brownouts can trigger false RAM failures.
safetyImpact: Affected body systems may be unreliable.

fixSteps.title: Test battery
fixSteps.instruction: Load test battery; verify >12.4V.

fixSteps.title: Check grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect and clean BCM ground points.

fixSteps.title: Replace BCM
fixSteps.instruction: Replace and program.

faq.q: Warranty?
faq.a: Check manufacturer powertrain/body warranty coverage.

title: BCM ROM Checksum Failure
shortDescription: BCM program memory has failed checksum verification.
fullDescription:
Code B1003 sets when the BCM cannot validate its internal program memory. This indicates corrupted firmware or a failed flash chip. Reprogramming may recover the module; otherwise replacement is required.

Brief power interruptions during an OTA update can leave the module in this state.
safetyImpact: BCM-controlled features may be unpredictable.

fixSteps.title: Attempt reflash
fixSteps.instruction: Reprogram with OEM software.

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: Install new BCM.

faq.q: DIY possible?
faq.a: Reflash needs OEM subscription; usually dealer job.

title: HVAC Control Head Internal Error
shortDescription: Climate control head has an internal fault.
fullDescription:
Code B1023 is set by the HVAC control module when it detects an internal error—often a failed button matrix, LCD driver, or rotary encoder. Functions such as temperature, fan, and mode selection may not respond.

Many control heads can be disassembled for cleaning contacts; persistent faults need a replacement unit coded to the vehicle.
safetyImpact: No direct safety impact; may reduce defrost function in some conditions.

fixSteps.title: Inspect panel
fixSteps.instruction: Remove dash trim; check connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace control head
fixSteps.instruction: Swap unit and code if required.

faq.q: Can I use aftermarket?
faq.a: OEM recommended for proper coding.

title: A/C Request Circuit Open
shortDescription: BCM detects an open in the A/C request signal to the PCM.
fullDescription:
Code B1028 indicates the A/C request wire from the BCM (or climate head) to the PCM is open. The PCM will not engage the A/C compressor clutch without this signal.

Check the wire continuity, connector pins, and BCM output driver.
