safetyImpact: No A/C cooling; defrost may be less effective in humid conditions.

fixSteps.title: Bidirectional command
fixSteps.instruction: Command A/C request on with scan tool; probe at PCM pin.

fixSteps.title: Repair wire
fixSteps.instruction: Fix open wire/connector.

faq.q: Is this a refrigerant issue?
faq.a: No—this is an electrical signal fault.

title: A/C Request Circuit Shorted
shortDescription: A/C request signal is shorted to ground or voltage.
fullDescription:
Code B1029 sets when the BCM detects the A/C request line at a voltage inconsistent with commanded state. Pinch damage or a chafed harness near the HVAC box is common.

Isolate and repair the wire with proper solder and heat-shrink.
safetyImpact: A/C may run continuously or not at all.
symptoms: A/C always on or always off

fixSteps.title: Isolate wire
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect both ends; test for shorts.

fixSteps.title: Repair harness
fixSteps.instruction: Replace damaged wire section.

faq.q: Safe to drive?
faq.a: Yes, but expect poor cabin comfort.

title: HVAC Blower Control Circuit Fault
shortDescription: Blower motor control signal from climate module is out of range.
fullDescription:
Code B1035 points to a problem in the PWM or speed-control signal sent from the climate control module to the blower power module. This may be an open, short, or a failed power module.

Test the drive signal and the blower motor itself before replacing the climate head.
safetyImpact: Cabin climate compromised.

fixSteps.title: Test blower direct
fixSteps.instruction: Apply 12V to motor; confirm it runs.

fixSteps.title: Replace power module
fixSteps.instruction: Most commonly bad part.

faq.q: Why does it burn out?
faq.a: High blower current stresses the module—replace both together if motor is sluggish.

title: HVAC Mode Door Actuator Fault
shortDescription: Mode door actuator position feedback is out of range.
fullDescription:
Code B1042 indicates the HVAC mode door actuator (which routes air between vents, floor, and defrost) is stuck or its position sensor is reporting invalid values. Common failure point on many vehicles; often heard as a repetitive clicking behind the dash.

A relearn procedure may restore operation briefly before the gear strips again.
safetyImpact: Defrost may be ineffective.

fixSteps.title: Re-calibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Run HVAC relearn with scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Replace actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Single part, usually accessible from glove box side.

faq.q: Why clicking?
faq.a: Actuator gear teeth stripped; motor keeps trying.

title: Temperature Blend Door Actuator Fault
shortDescription: Blend door actuator is not reaching commanded position.
fullDescription:
Code B1043 concerns the temperature blend door, which mixes hot and cold air. A failed actuator causes output air temperature to be stuck or reversed (cold when heat is commanded).

Dual-zone vehicles have two blend doors; confirm which side is at fault with scan tool data.
safetyImpact: Comfort impact only.
symptoms: Heat or A/C not mixing correctly
One side hot, one side cold on dual-zone

fixSteps.title: Access actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Remove lower dash panel.

fixSteps.title: Replace unit
fixSteps.instruction: Connect and run relearn.

faq.q: Dual zone?
faq.a: Yes—most vehicles have two blend doors.

title: Recirculation Door Actuator Fault
shortDescription: Recirculation door actuator has invalid feedback.
fullDescription:
Code B1048 signals a fault in the fresh-air/recirculation door actuator. The cabin may smell like exhaust if the door defaults open, or the A/C may be less effective if stuck on fresh.

Actuator is usually accessible from the passenger footwell.
safetyImpact: Reduced cabin air quality in traffic.

fixSteps.title: Test motion
fixSteps.instruction: Command positions with scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Actuator accessible under glove box.

title: A/C Evaporator Temp Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Evaporator temperature sensor circuit out of range.
fullDescription:
Code B1055 indicates the evaporator temperature sensor—used to prevent coil freezing—is reading implausibly high or low. The PCM may disable the compressor as a protection.

Sensor is a small thermistor clipped to the evaporator fins.
safetyImpact: A/C may cycle on/off or refuse to run.

fixSteps.title: Probe sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance vs. temperature chart.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Sensor clipped to evap fins.

title: Keyless Entry Module Internal Fault
shortDescription: RF receiver/transceiver module has an internal fault.
fullDescription:
Code B1505 is set by the vehicle when the keyless entry module itself fails its self-test. The module decodes rolling codes from the fob; a failure can disable all passive-entry/push-button-start functions.

Mechanical key or spare fob may still start the car depending on design.
safetyImpact: Vehicle may require mechanical key to start.

fixSteps.title: Confirm fob works
fixSteps.instruction: Try spare key fob.

fixSteps.title: Replace receiver
fixSteps.instruction: Usually under dash or behind rear trim; needs programming.

title: Left Front Door Lock Actuator Circuit
shortDescription: BCM detects open or short in LF door lock actuator circuit.
fullDescription:
Code B1515 indicates a fault in the driver-side door lock motor circuit. The actuator may be seized, or the circuit may have chafed inside the door boot between chassis and door.

The door may not lock/unlock via the switch or fob; manual key still works.
safetyImpact: Door may not lock electrically—security concern.

causes.cause: Broken wire in door jamb boot

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test
fixSteps.instruction: Flex harness at boot while commanding lock.

fixSteps.title: Repair harness
fixSteps.instruction: Splice broken wires in boot.

fixSteps.title: Replace actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Remove door panel; swap motor assembly.

title: Right Front Door Lock Actuator Circuit
shortDescription: Passenger front door lock circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B1516 is analogous to B1515 for the passenger-front door. Same symptoms and diagnosis process apply.

Integrated latch-plus-actuator assemblies are typical on modern vehicles.
safetyImpact: Security concern only.
symptoms: Passenger door won't lock from switch

fixSteps.title: Flex boot
fixSteps.instruction: Check wire continuity while flexing.

fixSteps.title: Replace actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Pull door panel.

title: Left Rear Door Lock Actuator Circuit
shortDescription: LR door lock actuator circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B1517 indicates a fault on the left rear door lock. Typical cause is a broken wire in the door boot from repeated flexing.

Soldered repair with heat shrink is more reliable than crimp splices in boot areas.
safetyImpact: Security concern only.

fixSteps.title: Harness repair
fixSteps.instruction: Fix wire at pivot.

fixSteps.title: Replace actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear door panel.

title: Right Rear Door Lock Actuator Circuit
shortDescription: RR door lock actuator circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B1518 indicates a right-rear door lock circuit fault. Same repair pattern as other doors.

Look for repeated codes across multiple doors that would indicate a common BCM output issue.
safetyImpact: Security concern only.

fixSteps.title: Boot inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Flex-test the harness.

fixSteps.title: Replace unit
fixSteps.instruction: Swap actuator in door.

title: Memory Seat Position Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Memory seat motor position sensor out of range.
fullDescription:
Code B1525 is set when one of the position sensors in a memory driver seat reports invalid data. Memory recall may not work, or the seat may move to the wrong position.

Motor/sensor assemblies are built into the seat rails and are replaced as a unit on most vehicles.
safetyImpact: Comfort feature only.

fixSteps.title: Identify axis
fixSteps.instruction: Scan tool shows which motor.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor/sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Seat off vehicle.

title: Driver Window Switch Circuit Fault
shortDescription: Driver master switch reports implausible input.
fullDescription:
Code B1540 indicates the BCM has detected a short or open in the driver master window switch pack. Most commonly caused by water intrusion via the door vapor barrier or a failed LF window switch module.

Inspect the plastic vapor barrier—a torn one lets water drip directly on the switch.
safetyImpact: Windows may operate erratically.
symptoms: Multiple windows won't operate from driver

fixSteps.title: Dry and clean switch
fixSteps.instruction: Disassemble if possible.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch pack
fixSteps.instruction: Plug-and-play part.

title: Left Rear Window Motor Circuit
shortDescription: LR window motor circuit open/short.
fullDescription:
Code B1548 is set when the left rear window motor circuit draws improper current. Regulator or motor may have failed, or the wire in the door boot is broken.

Plastic regulator clips are a frequent weak point.
safetyImpact: Window may be stuck.

fixSteps.title: Door panel off
fixSteps.instruction: Test motor directly.

fixSteps.title: Replace regulator
fixSteps.instruction: Most fail with plastic clips.

title: Key Fob Low Battery
shortDescription: Keyless module has detected the paired fob's battery is low.
fullDescription:
Code B1555 is informational—most vehicles use it to trigger a driver display message. Replace the CR2032 (or similar) coin cell in the fob. The code will clear automatically after a few successful transmissions.

Carry a spare coin cell for convenience.
safetyImpact: None.

fixSteps.title: Replace coin cell
fixSteps.instruction: Pop fob apart, swap battery.

faq.q: Re-learn needed?
faq.a: No—same fob, just new battery.

title: Cabin Air Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: In-car temperature sensor out of range.
fullDescription:
Code B2215 concerns the aspirated in-car temperature sensor. If blocked or failed, automatic climate control will misread cabin temperature and run heat or A/C excessively.

Aspirator tubing can become clogged with dust.
safetyImpact: Comfort only.
symptoms: Display shows obviously wrong cabin temp

fixSteps.title: Clean aspirator
fixSteps.instruction: Blow out tube.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Behind dash panel.

title: Rear Blower Motor Circuit Fault
shortDescription: Rear HVAC blower motor circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B2230 indicates the rear HVAC blower circuit is open, shorted, or drawing abnormal current. Minivans and SUVs with rear climate commonly set this when the rear motor fails.

Debris from rear cargo often causes rear blower failures.
safetyImpact: Rear passengers uncomfortable.

fixSteps.title: Access rear blower
fixSteps.instruction: Behind rear quarter trim typically.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Direct swap.

title: Refrigerant Pressure Sensor Fault
shortDescription: A/C high-side pressure transducer out of range.
fullDescription:
Code B2250 indicates the pressure transducer on the high side of the A/C system is reporting values outside its plausible range. The PCM may disable the compressor as a protective measure.

Schrader-style transducers can be swapped without venting refrigerant.
safetyImpact: No cabin cooling.

fixSteps.title: Gauge the system
fixSteps.instruction: Compare to manifold readings.

fixSteps.title: Replace transducer
fixSteps.instruction: Schrader-style—no recharge needed on most systems.

title: Secondary Distribution Door Actuator
shortDescription: Secondary air distribution door actuator feedback out of range.
fullDescription:
Code B2265 identifies a fault with a secondary distribution door (often for defrost-only or dual-zone splits). Symptoms include air coming from the wrong vents.

On some vehicles this is buried deep in the dash and is a labor-intensive repair.
safetyImpact: Defrost may be weak.

fixSteps.title: Replace actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Behind dash; relearn required.

title: Driver Heated Seat Circuit Fault
shortDescription: Driver heated seat element or module circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B2280 is commonly set when the heating element in the driver seat cushion or backrest has an open circuit. Replacement of the element or full cushion cover is often required.

Labor is significant—skilled upholstery work.
safetyImpact: Comfort only.

fixSteps.title: Measure resistance
fixSteps.instruction: At seat connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace element/cover
fixSteps.instruction: Labor intensive.

title: Passenger Heated Seat Circuit
shortDescription: Passenger heated seat circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B2281 is the passenger analog of B2280.

Often both front seat elements fail within a similar timeframe; consider doing both at once.
safetyImpact: Comfort only.

fixSteps.title: Measure element
fixSteps.instruction: At connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace element
fixSteps.instruction: Cover removal required.

title: Trunk Release Switch Circuit
shortDescription: Trunk release switch input stuck or shorted.
fullDescription:
Code B2310 indicates the trunk release switch is always-on or wired short. The trunk lid may pop open spuriously.

Rain water through a leaking dash can short these switches.
safetyImpact: Security/cargo concern.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect switch
fixSteps.instruction: See if code clears.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Behind dash trim.

title: Trunk Latch Motor Circuit
shortDescription: Electric trunk latch motor circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B2320 indicates a fault in the powered trunk latch that pulls the lid fully closed (soft-close) or pops it open. The motor or latch assembly usually needs replacement.

Check the weatherstrip first—a swollen seal can prevent the latch from reaching its closed microswitch.
safetyImpact: Trunk may not latch reliably.

fixSteps.title: Replace latch
fixSteps.instruction: Unit under trunk lid trim.

title: Power Liftgate Drive Motor Circuit
shortDescription: Power liftgate motor/strut circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B2340 is set when a power liftgate motor (or electric strut) circuit draws improper current or a position sensor is out of range. Common on SUVs with power tailgates.

Manual operation of the gate may cause the motor to resist; always fully release the power system before manual use.
safetyImpact: Liftgate must be operated manually.

fixSteps.title: Diagnose side
fixSteps.instruction: Scan tool shows which motor.

fixSteps.title: Replace strut
fixSteps.instruction: Remove trim; unclip unit.

title: Liftgate Pinch/Obstruction Sensor
shortDescription: Liftgate obstruction sensor circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B2345 relates to the strip or pressure sensor used to detect obstructions while the power liftgate is closing. When faulty, the gate may refuse to close or close without obstruction detection.

Installing aftermarket strips can be tricky—ensure full-length contact with the gate edge.
safetyImpact: Pinch protection may be disabled.

fixSteps.title: Inspect strip
fixSteps.instruction: Visible along gate edge.

fixSteps.title: Replace strip
fixSteps.instruction: Peel off old, install new.

title: Trailer Brake Controller Circuit Fault
shortDescription: Integrated trailer brake controller output circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B2355 is set when an integrated trailer brake controller (found on many OEM tow packages) detects an open or short in its output to the trailer. May be caused by a disconnected trailer plug or damaged pin.

Check both the truck's 7-pin socket and the trailer's plug for corrosion.
safetyImpact: Trailer brakes may not function—significant stopping distance increase with a loaded trailer.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Clean pins at tow hitch plug.

fixSteps.title: Test trailer
fixSteps.instruction: Isolate to truck or trailer.

fixSteps.title: Replace controller
fixSteps.instruction: Dash unit.

faq.q: Safe to tow?
faq.a: No, tow only after repair.

title: Interior Courtesy Lamp Driver Fault
shortDescription: BCM courtesy lamp driver has an internal fault or overload.
fullDescription:
Code B2430 indicates the interior courtesy lamp output driver has detected an overload. After the overload is removed, the code may need to be manually cleared. Repeated short-to-ground events can permanently damage the BCM driver.

Isolate each lamp on the circuit to find the offender.
safetyImpact: Interior lights may not work.

fixSteps.title: Isolate short
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug dome, headliner map lights one at a time.

fixSteps.title: Replace/repair
fixSteps.instruction: Swap offending lamp or BCM.

title: Headlamp Leveling Motor Circuit
shortDescription: Electric headlamp leveling motor circuit out of range.
fullDescription:
Code B2455 sets when a headlamp level-adjustment motor fails. On vehicles with HID/LED lamps, this leveling is mandated; a failure will often force the lamps into a safe low position.

Motors are serviceable on most vehicles without replacing the whole headlight.
safetyImpact: Potentially reduced night visibility.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Small motor attached to reflector.

title: Automatic Headlamp/Rain Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Automatic headlamp light sensor circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B2470 indicates that the windshield-mounted sensor module (often combining rain and light sensors) is failing communication or power. The automatic headlamp and automatic wipers may not function.

The gel pad that couples the sensor to the windshield must be replaced any time the sensor is removed.
safetyImpact: Headlamps may need manual operation.
symptoms: Auto headlamps don't activate at dusk

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Check gel pad contact.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor module
fixSteps.instruction: Unclip from windshield; re-bond gel.

title: Radio/Head Unit Display Communication Fault
shortDescription: Infotainment head unit has lost communication with the display module.
fullDescription:
Code B2905 indicates the infotainment system's main unit cannot communicate with its display head. This is common on vehicles with separate display and controller modules linked by a dedicated bus or LVDS.

Video-out cables are often the culprit; module replacement is expensive.
safetyImpact: Infotainment inoperative; audio may still work.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cable
fixSteps.instruction: Access behind head unit.

fixSteps.title: Swap display
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm with known-good unit.

title: Audio Amplifier Communication Fault
shortDescription: Head unit has lost communication with the external amplifier.
fullDescription:
Code B2915 is set when a separately-housed audio amplifier (Bose, JBL, B&O, etc.) does not respond on the MOST or media bus. Fiber-optic MOST rings are easily broken at connectors.

Diagnosis requires a MOST-capable scan tool or a replacement amplifier.
safetyImpact: No audio at all if MOST ring broken.

fixSteps.title: Ring diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: Scan tool shows first offline node.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fiber
fixSteps.instruction: Check connector faces for damage.

fixSteps.title: Replace amp
fixSteps.instruction: Last resort.

title: Front Left Speaker Circuit Shorted
shortDescription: Amplifier detects short on front left speaker output.
fullDescription:
Code B2930 means the amplifier has muted the front-left channel because it detected a short or very low-impedance load. Common cause is a torn speaker cone contacting the voice coil or a pinched speaker wire.

Measure DC resistance at the speaker—should be 2-4 ohms typically.
safetyImpact: Audio quality reduced.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect speaker
fixSteps.instruction: See if other channels recover.

fixSteps.title: Replace speaker
fixSteps.instruction: Door panel off.

title: Steering Wheel Cruise Switch Circuit
shortDescription: Cruise switch circuit on steering wheel out of range.
fullDescription:
Code B2945 sets when the cruise-control switch resistor ladder reports implausible resistance. May be accompanied by inability to set or resume cruise control.

Clockspring replacement requires SRS safety procedure.
safetyImpact: Cruise control unavailable.

fixSteps.title: Test at connector
fixSteps.instruction: Compare to service data resistance table.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Wheel switch pod.

title: Horn Relay Control Circuit Fault
shortDescription: BCM horn relay drive circuit open or shorted.
fullDescription:
Code B2955 indicates the BCM output that drives the horn relay is not responding correctly. The horn may not sound or sound continuously.

Most horn relays are interchangeable with other accessory relays—swap to test.
safetyImpact: Horn is a federally required safety device.

fixSteps.title: Swap relay
fixSteps.instruction: Relay identical to other accessory relays often.

fixSteps.title: Repair wire
fixSteps.instruction: Trace wire to BCM.

title: Antenna Amplifier Power Circuit
shortDescription: Powered antenna amplifier circuit open or shorted.
fullDescription:
Code B3005 indicates the powered antenna module (often in the rear window or shark-fin) has lost power or is drawing too much current. FM/AM/GPS/SDARS reception may suffer depending on which amplifier.

Replace the amplifier rather than the whole glass on most vehicles.
safetyImpact: Reduced radio reception.

fixSteps.title: Check power at amp
fixSteps.instruction: Measure at connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace amplifier
fixSteps.instruction: On glass or roof.

title: Subwoofer Output Circuit Fault
shortDescription: Amplifier detects subwoofer output fault.
fullDescription:
Code B3115 indicates a fault on the subwoofer output channel—either a blown driver, shorted voice coil, or open wire. Bass response will be absent or distorted.

A blown sub can sometimes be confirmed visually by a torn surround.
safetyImpact: Audio quality only.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect sub
fixSteps.instruction: Clears fault if sub is at fault.

fixSteps.title: Replace subwoofer
fixSteps.instruction: Trunk/rear shelf mounted.

title: Navigation/Media Disc Reader Fault
shortDescription: Optical disc drive in head unit reports internal fault.
fullDescription:
Code B3205 is set by legacy navigation/CD/DVD units when the laser pickup fails. Older vehicles may still use map DVDs; a replacement unit or laser assembly is required.

Some aftermarket retrofits avoid the disc by bridging to a USB/SD input.
safetyImpact: Navigation/media unavailable.

fixSteps.title: Clean lens
fixSteps.instruction: Lens cleaner disc.

fixSteps.title: Replace head unit
fixSteps.instruction: If cleaning fails.

title: Bluetooth/Telematics Module Fault
shortDescription: Bluetooth/HF module internal fault.
fullDescription:
Code B3320 indicates the hands-free Bluetooth module has an internal fault or has lost its pairing database. On some vehicles the module is integrated with the telematics unit.

Try clearing pairings and re-pairing before replacing.
safetyImpact: Hands-free calling unavailable.

fixSteps.title: Clear pairings
fixSteps.instruction: Delete all on car and phone, re-pair.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer software update.

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: Usually under dash.

title: USB Hub Port Circuit Fault
shortDescription: USB port overcurrent or short detected.
fullDescription:
Code B3415 sets when an in-cabin USB charging/data port is overloaded or shorted. Bent pins in the port from a stuck cable are typical.

BCM output drivers are often self-resetting but may latch off until code clears.
safetyImpact: None.

fixSteps.title: Inspect port
fixSteps.instruction: Look for bent/missing pins.

fixSteps.title: Replace port
fixSteps.instruction: Clip-in part on most cars.

title: Sunroof/Moonroof Motor Circuit Fault
shortDescription: Sunroof motor circuit draws abnormal current.
fullDescription:
Code B3710 is set when the moonroof motor is drawing excessive current (binding mechanism) or an open is detected. Common cause is a dirty/dry sunroof track where the glass panel binds on its guides.

Use only silicone-based lubricant—petroleum grease attracts more dust.
safetyImpact: May be stuck open—exposure to weather possible.

fixSteps.title: Clean and lube tracks
fixSteps.instruction: Use silicone grease—no petroleum.

fixSteps.title: Replace cables/motor
fixSteps.instruction: Major headliner job.

title: Sunroof Position Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Sunroof position sensor out of range or implausible.
fullDescription:
Code B3715 indicates the position encoder on the moonroof motor is not reporting correctly. One-touch and pinch protection may be disabled.

A full close-and-hold cycle usually relearns position after battery disconnect.
safetyImpact: Pinch protection may be disabled.

fixSteps.title: Run relearn
fixSteps.instruction: Hold close button until full cycle completes.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor with encoder
fixSteps.instruction: Under headliner.

title: Powered Sunshade Motor Circuit
shortDescription: Power sunshade motor circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B3720 is set when a separate powered sunshade (under the glass panel) has a motor or sensor fault. On luxury vehicles this is a distinct motor from the glass itself.

Labor is substantial—headliner must drop.
safetyImpact: Comfort only.

fixSteps.title: Replace shade motor
fixSteps.instruction: Part of shade assembly.

title: Convertible Top Hydraulic Pump Circuit
shortDescription: Convertible top motor/pump circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B3810 indicates the electric-hydraulic pump that raises and lowers a convertible top is not working correctly. Causes include a failed pump motor, low hydraulic fluid, or a wiring fault in the trunk area.

Check reservoir fluid level before condemning the pump.
safetyImpact: Top may be stuck partially open/closed, risk of weather exposure.
symptoms: Pump runs but top doesn't move

fixSteps.title: Check fluid
fixSteps.instruction: Locate pump reservoir.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump
fixSteps.instruction: Trunk-mounted.

title: Convertible Top Position Switch Fault
shortDescription: Convertible top latch/position switch input invalid.
fullDescription:
Code B3820 indicates one of the several microswitches that monitor convertible top position has failed or is out of adjustment. The top may refuse to move because the control module can't verify a valid state.

Scan tool data shows each switch's state during operation.
safetyImpact: Top stuck.

fixSteps.title: Identify switch
fixSteps.instruction: Scan tool shows which position isn't confirming.

fixSteps.title: Adjust or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Small switch on frame.

title: Convertible Top Latch Motor Circuit
shortDescription: Convertible top header latch motor circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Code B3830 concerns the motorized latches that secure the convertible top to the windshield header. A failed motor or limit switch prevents full lock; the vehicle may refuse to move the top further.

Use the emergency manual release if stranded with an open top.
safetyImpact: Top may not secure to header.

fixSteps.title: Manual release
fixSteps.instruction: Use emergency release to unlatch.

fixSteps.title: Replace latch assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Bolted to header.

title: Floor/Foot Air Door Actuator Fault
shortDescription: Foot air door actuator feedback out of range.
fullDescription: Code B1044 indicates the floor-discharge air door actuator is stuck or reporting invalid position. Heated air may not reach the foot well properly.
safetyImpact: Comfort only.

fixSteps.title: Relearn HVAC
fixSteps.instruction: Scan tool routine.

fixSteps.title: Replace actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Under dash.

title: Interior Motion/Intrusion Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Interior alarm motion sensor circuit fault.
fullDescription: Code B1560 indicates the cabin motion/ultrasonic intrusion sensor (often in the headliner) has an electrical fault. The alarm system's interior monitoring function is disabled, but perimeter alarm still works.
safetyImpact: Reduced alarm sensitivity.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Clipped into headliner.

title: Hood Ajar Switch Circuit Fault
shortDescription: Hood ajar switch input implausible.
fullDescription: Code B1575 sets when the hood switch (used for alarm and sometimes for crash-sensing) is stuck or shorted. Alarm may trigger spuriously or not at all when hood is opened.
safetyImpact: Alarm function impaired.

fixSteps.title: Adjust switch
fixSteps.instruction: Bend contact to proper height.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Small part on fender/radiator support.

title: DRL Output Circuit Short to Ground
shortDescription: Daytime running lamp output shorted.
fullDescription: Code B2480 sets when the BCM's daytime running lamp output detects a short to ground. DRL may be disabled; headlamp may still work in manual mode.
safetyImpact: DRL unavailable.

fixSteps.title: Isolate short
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug each DRL socket.

fixSteps.title: Replace damaged part
fixSteps.instruction: Socket, bulb, or harness.

title: SiriusXM/Satellite Radio Module Fault
shortDescription: Satellite radio tuner module internal fault.
fullDescription: Code B3025 indicates the satellite radio tuner module (SDARS) has an internal fault. AM/FM/Bluetooth may still function.
safetyImpact: None.
symptoms: No satellite radio reception with subscription active

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: Often under rear parcel shelf.

title: Center Dash Speaker Output Shorted
shortDescription: Amplifier detects center speaker short.
fullDescription: Code B3150 sets when the center-channel dash speaker output is shorted. Center-channel dialog and voice prompts may be absent.
safetyImpact: Audio only.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect center
fixSteps.instruction: Amp should recover.

fixSteps.title: Replace speaker
fixSteps.instruction: Under dash top.

title: Qi Wireless Charging Pad Fault
shortDescription: Wireless charging pad module fault.
fullDescription: Code B3455 indicates the in-dash wireless phone charger has reported an internal fault or overheating shutdown. Charging will be disabled until code clears.
safetyImpact: None.
symptoms: Phone gets warm, fails to charge

fixSteps.title: Clear pad
fixSteps.instruction: Remove any metal debris.

fixSteps.title: Replace unit
fixSteps.instruction: Bolted in console.

title: SBEC/BCM VIN Mismatch
shortDescription: Stored VIN between modules does not match.
fullDescription: Code B1105 sets when a replacement module's VIN doesn't match the other modules. Reprogram with correct VIN.
safetyImpact: None once synced.
symptoms: Multiple warning lights after module swap

fixSteps.title: Program VIN
fixSteps.instruction: OEM procedure.

title: Glass-Break Alarm Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Glass-break sensor circuit fault.
fullDescription: Code B1620 indicates the glass-break sensor used by the alarm system has an electrical fault. Perimeter audio detection of breaking glass is disabled.
safetyImpact: Reduced alarm sensitivity.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Located in headliner or pillar.

title: Panoramic Sunroof Rear Glass Motor
shortDescription: Rear panel motor on panoramic sunroof has circuit fault.
fullDescription: Code B3725 applies to panoramic sunroofs with a separate rear glass panel. The rear motor circuit is open or shorted. Rear panel can't be operated.
safetyImpact: Partial function only.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Accessible after headliner drop.

title: Convertible Top Storage Cover Motor
shortDescription: Tonneau/storage cover motor circuit fault on convertible.
fullDescription:
Code B3890 sets when the powered tonneau cover (which conceals the stowed convertible top) motor circuit has an open, short, or excessive current draw. The top-operation sequence aborts because the cover cannot move to allow top travel.

Inspect motor wiring at the rear flex point and check the cover hinges for binding.
safetyImpact: Top operation disabled; vehicle stuck in current configuration.

fixSteps.title: Check hinges
fixSteps.instruction: Lubricate and verify cover moves freely by hand.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Access via trunk trim.

title: ECU Malfunction - Airbag System

title: Hood Switch Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: Body-side circuit fault: hood switch circuit malfunction.
fullDescription:
B1057 indicates a fault in a body-side circuit that interfaces with the engine compartment. Although the affected component sits near the engine, the fault is logged by the body controller because that module owns the circuit.

Wiring routed between the cabin and engine bay is exposed to heat, moisture, and chafing. Most B105x-B110x faults are connector or harness issues rather than failed components.

A careful pin-fit and resistance check at the BCM connector usually localizes the problem within minutes once you have a wiring diagram.
safetyImpact: Generally low-impact, but related accessory features may not work correctly.

causes.cause: Damaged or chafed harness in engine bay

fixSteps.title: Read freeze frame
fixSteps.instruction: Capture freeze-frame data when hood fault was last active to identify operating conditions.

fixSteps.title: Inspect circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Visually inspect the hood wiring, connector, and component for damage, corrosion, or moisture intrusion.

fixSteps.title: Test component
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance and supply voltage at the hood component and compare to factory specification.

fixSteps.title: Replace and verify
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the failed hood component or repair the circuit, then clear codes and confirm the fault does not return.

faq.q: Will this code clear itself?
faq.a: It may go inactive if the fault is intermittent, but the history will remain stored until cleared with a scan tool.

title: Headlamp Leveling Motor Left Circuit
shortDescription: Exterior lighting circuit fault: headlamp leveling motor left circuit.
fullDescription:
B1402 is set when the body controller detects an electrical problem in the headlamp leveling motor left circuit circuit. The BCM monitors lamp current and reports open-circuit, shorted, or out-of-range conditions.

Lighting circuits fail predictably: bulbs first, then sockets, then connectors, and finally the driver inside the BCM. Always verify the bulb and socket ground before condemning the module.

LED-based assemblies often store this code when a single LED string fails inside a sealed unit, requiring full assembly replacement.
safetyImpact: Reduced visibility for the driver and reduced visibility of the vehicle to others, especially at night.

fixSteps.title: Replace and verify
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the failed lamp circuit component or repair the circuit, then clear codes and confirm the fault does not return.

faq.a: Yes for short distances, but most jurisdictions require all lights to be functional. Repair before night driving.

title: Speedometer Stepper Motor Failure
shortDescription: Instrument cluster fault: speedometer stepper motor failure.
fullDescription:
B3110 is set by the instrument cluster module when it detects an internal hardware problem. Modern clusters combine analog gauges, color displays, and warning indicators in a single sealed assembly.

Stepper motor faults are particularly common on older clusters as the motors age and lose torque. Symptoms include needles that sweep incorrectly at startup, stop short of full scale, or freeze in place.

Most cluster repairs require either reflashing, stepper motor replacement, or full cluster swap and odometer reprogramming through the manufacturer's tool.
safetyImpact: Inaccurate gauges can mask serious mechanical issues. Treat fuel and coolant gauge failures as high priority even though the code itself is low severity.

causes.cause: Cold solder joints on cluster PCB

title: Sunroof Motor Circuit Open
shortDescription: Roof system fault: sunroof motor circuit open.
fullDescription:
B3705 is reported by the body or roof controller when it detects a fault in the sunroof or convertible top system. These systems combine motors, hydraulics, position sensors and safety interlocks.

Most sunroof faults trace back to drainage problems: clogged drains let water reach the motor, harness or controller. Convertible top faults often start in the hydraulic system as seals age and pressure drops below the threshold needed to complete a cycle.

Safety interlocks (anti-pinch, latch confirmation) are intentionally strict. A single failed sensor will disable motion of the entire roof until the fault is resolved.
safetyImpact: Roof feature inoperative; if stuck open, vehicle becomes vulnerable to weather and theft.
symptoms: Roof does not open or close

title: Sunshade Motor Circuit Failure
shortDescription: Roof system fault: sunshade motor circuit failure.
fullDescription:
B3735 is reported by the body or roof controller when it detects a fault in the sunroof or convertible top system. These systems combine motors, hydraulics, position sensors and safety interlocks.

Most sunroof faults trace back to drainage problems: clogged drains let water reach the motor, harness or controller. Convertible top faults often start in the hydraulic system as seals age and pressure drops below the threshold needed to complete a cycle.

Safety interlocks (anti-pinch, latch confirmation) are intentionally strict. A single failed sensor will disable motion of the entire roof until the fault is resolved.
safetyImpact: Roof feature inoperative; if stuck open, vehicle becomes vulnerable to weather and theft.
symptoms: Roof does not open or close
